BURHAN:v3p471/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p471/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p471/r3.claim: The phrase about what is before and behind exhausts the categories of time, leaving no fourth category.
BURHAN:v3p471/r3.anchor: كذلك قوله تعالى ﴿ له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا ﴾ 3

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r1.claim: A report says Gabriel once delayed visiting the Prophet; when he came, the Prophet said he missed him and asked whether he might visit more often, after which the verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r1.anchor: أبطأ جبريل عن الرسول مرة، فلما جاء قال: «يا جبريل قد اشتقت إليك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r2.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk connect the revelation to Gabriel's delay in answering the questions discussed in Sūrat al-Kahf, comparing it with al-Ḍuḥā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك: سببها أن جبريل عليه السلام تأخر في السؤالات المتقدمة في سورة الكهف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r3.claim: Tanazzul may express gradual, repeated action after nuzzaltuhu, or simply mean nazala without a sense of gradual continuation; a poetic line illustrates ordinary descent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r3.anchor: وتنزل تفعل وهي للمطاوعة وهي أحد معاني تفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives tanazzul two senses, descent gradually or descent generally, and takes gradual descent as appropriate here, describing visits spaced over time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r4.anchor: التنزل على معنيين: معنى النزول على مهل، ومعنى النزول على الإطلاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the wāw links one sentence to another without requiring the two statements to have identical meanings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r5.anchor: وهذه الواو التي في قوله وما نتنزل هي عاطفة جملة كلام على أخرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r6.speaker: النقاش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r6.claim: Al-Naqqāsh attributes to some a weak view that the verse continues Gabriel's words to Mary, beginning 'I am only your Lord's messenger.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r6.anchor: وحكى النقاش عن قوم أن قوله وما نتنزل متصل بقوله إنما أنا رسول ربك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r7.claim: The verse closes the stories of favored prophets and their descendants, then addresses Muḥammad, himself descended from Abraham; the negligent successors were scriptural communities whose behavior caused Quraysh and Jews to question the Prophet, and the delay pleased them. Gabriel explains that revelation's timing belongs to God, absolving himself; the verse states the result rather than the worldly desire and hidden malice that caused it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p280/r7.anchor: والذي يظهر في مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها أنه تعالى لما ذكر قصة زكريا ومريم وذكر إبراهيم وموسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya takes 'before us' as the world up to the first blast, 'behind us' as the afterlife from resurrection, and 'between' as the interval between the two blasts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r1.anchor: قال أبو العالية: ما بين الأيدي الدنيا بأسرها إلى النفخة الأولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Abū al-ʿĀliya's explanation fits human beings, whereas the speech belongs to angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r2.anchor: وقول أبي العالية إنما يتصور في بني آدم، وهذه المقالة هي للملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says what is before them is time before creation, behind them is after death through the eternal afterlife, and between is lifetime.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: ما بين الأيدي هو ما مر من الزمان قبل الإيجاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r4.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس وابن جبير وقتادة ومقاتل وسفيان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r4.claim: They reverse the spatial labels: before is the afterlife, behind is this world, with the interval between them in between.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r4.anchor: ما بين أيدينا الآخرة وما خلفنا الدنيا رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r5.claim: Mujāhid gives the opposite mapping from the preceding report.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r6.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash takes before as before creation, behind as after annihilation, and between as the span from this world to the next; elsewhere he says 'between' means their present state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r6.anchor: وقال الأخفش: ما بين أيدينا قبل أن نخلق وما خلفنا بعد الفناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r7.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة وأبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r7.claim: They also identify 'between' as the time between the two trumpet blasts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة وأبو العالية: ما بين النفختين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r8.speaker: صاحب الغينان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r8.claim: The author of al-Ghīnān says before is the angels' descent from heaven, behind is the earth, and between is the space from heaven to earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r8.anchor: وقال صاحب الغينان: ما بين أيدينا نزول الملائكة من السماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r9.speaker: ابن القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r9.claim: Ibn al-Qushayrī adopts Ibn Jurayj's view and summarizes the three times as all belonging to God, who creates and directs them and controls when revelation descends.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r9.anchor: حصر الأزمنة الثلاثة وهي أن كلها لله هو منشئها ومدبر أمرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the point is God's ownership of the angels: all their movement and activity occurs by His wisdom and command; before, behind, and between may denote their locations and stations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r10.anchor: إنما القصد الإشعار بملك الله تعالى لملائكته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī likewise understands the words spatially: angels cannot move from one place or direction to another except by the King's command, for He encompasses everything.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r11.anchor: ما قدامنا وما خلفنا من الجهات والأماكن. وما نحن فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r12.speaker: البغوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r12.claim: Al-Baghawī interprets 'to Him belongs' as meaning that He knows what is before them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p281/r12.anchor: وقال البغوي: له علم ما بين أيدينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم وابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r1.claim: Abū Muslim and Ibn Baḥr say 'We do not descend' is not the angels' speech but the people of Paradise speaking to each other; the verses describe entry into Paradise and what lies before, behind, and between the two lives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r1.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم وابن بحر: وما نتنزل الآية ليس من كلام الملائكة وإنما هو من كلام أهل الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also reports that the pious say they enter Paradise only with God's permission and reward; God owns past, present, and future and enables good deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r2.anchor: وقيل هي حكاية قول المتقين حين يدخلون الجنة أي وما ننزل الجنة إلا بإذن من الله علينا بثواب أعمالنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r3.claim: God is not forgetful of workers or unaware of the reward due them; forgetfulness is impossible for the Lord of the heavens, earth, and all between them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r3.anchor: وما كان ربك نسيا لأعمال العاملين غافلا عما يجب أن يثابوا به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r4.speaker: القاضي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī rejects the paradise-speaker interpretation: the apparent descent is angels coming to the Prophet, the singular addressee does not suit a group speaking among themselves, and the following description of the Lord does not fit that scene.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r5.claim: The majority read tanazzalu with nūn, referring to Gabriel and the angels; al-Aʿraj reads yāʾ as a statement from God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور وما نتنزل بالنون عنى جبريل نفسه والملائكة. وقرأ الأعرج بالياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r6.claim: One explanation makes the yāʾ verb refer to Gabriel; Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that the following words 'to Him belong what is before us' do not fit this smoothly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r6.anchor: قيل: والضمير في يتنزل عائد على جبريل عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the better reading is a report from Gabriel that the Qur'an descends only when God sets its time; al-Zamakhsharī also treats it as Gabriel's speech, with the pronoun referring to revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r7.anchor: وإنما يتجه أن يكون خبرا عن جبريل أن القرآن لا يتنزل إلا بأمر الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r8.claim: The report can be understood as Gabriel saying that he descends only by God's command and that God controls the angels; he excuses the delay and assures Muḥammad that God has not forgotten him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p282/r8.anchor: ويحمل ذلك القول على إضمار أي وما يتنزل جبريل إلا بأمر ربك قائلا له ما بين أيدينا

STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r13.claim: The surah moves from revelation by God’s command to criticism of the Prophet and Quran, rejects claims God has a child, and ends with the silence of destroyed generations.
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r13.anchor: After a reminder in v. 64 that revelation only comes to the Prophet by God’s Command, the sūrah proceeds to address the criticisms leveled against the Prophet and the Quranic message

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Gabriel’s speech urges the Prophet to wait steadfastly for God’s decree and not hurry.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Through the tongue of Gabriel, the Prophet (sws) is directed to be patient and wait for the decree of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The closing passage first calls the Prophet to steadfastness, rebukes deniers of Judgment and their worldly-status argument, then directs him to warn and give glad tidings through the Qur’an and explain the fate of the obdurate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: First, through the tongue of Gabriel, the Prophet (sws) is urged to be steadfast. After that, the rejecters of the Day of Judgement are rebuked.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Gabriel’s words urge patience and clarify that he and the angels have no independent agency: they only follow God’s commands.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God’s directives. There is a special background to this advice and explanation given by him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Because revelation is the Prophet’s support in conflict, he naturally awaits Gabriel anxiously; like a soldier awaiting guidance, he must wait for help at its appointed time, as Qur’anic instruction elsewhere also teaches.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the sole support for the Prophet (sws) against his opponents in this phase of conflict with his opponents was divine revelation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Gabriel effectively apologizes that angels descend and bring revelation only at God’s command, so delay is not their fault and they cannot act independently.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Gabriel has actually presented a type of apology to the Prophet (sws) that his coming with divine revelation is based on God’s command

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The angels’ total subordination rebuts Arab polytheists who worshipped them as God’s daughters and expected their intercession; if even Gabriel is powerless, other angels have still less power.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the reason for explaining this status of the angels was to refute the notion of the Arab polytheists who worshipped angels

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The assurance that the Lord forgets nothing comforts the Prophet that no angel can exploit a lapse in awareness to carry out a plan independently.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God is not forgetful that anyone of them can use this forgetfulness to his advantage and implement his own will

BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r1.claim: Mujahid reports that Gabriel delayed his visit and cited neglected nail and moustache trimming, cleaning finger joints, and tooth-stick practice before reciting this verse.
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد : أبطأ الملك على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أتاه فقال له

BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r2.claim: A prophetic report commands cleaning finger joints where grime collects; al-Qurtubi says hardened dirt can retain impurity and block water from the skin.
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث : "نقوا براجمكم" وهي مفاصل الأصابع والعقد التي على ظهرها

BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r3.claim: Some exegetes connect the verse with questions about the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; revelation was delayed fifteen or forty days while the Prophet awaited an answer.
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : هو حكاية لقول جبريل حين استبطأه رسول الله

BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r4.speaker: جبريل
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r4.claim: Gabriel says he is a commanded servant: when sent he descends, and when held back he waits; the verse and Surat al-Duha then came down.
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r4.anchor: فقال جبريل : إني كنت أشوق ولكني عبد مأمور إذا بعثت نزلت

BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r5.claim: Tanazzul is gradual descent; angels descend only at God's command and when His wisdom requires it.
BURSEVI:v5p266#2/r5.anchor: والتنزل النزول على مهل لأنه مطاوع للتنزيل والمعنى قال الله لجبريل

BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r1.claim: What lies ahead means future afterlife affairs, what is behind means past worldly affairs, and what lies between means the present until Resurrection.
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r1.anchor: أي : بالاختصاص {ما بين أيدينا} من الأمور الأخروية الآتية

BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r2.claim: The inward reading interprets the phrases as eternal decree, everlasting governance, and everything between pre-eternity and eternity.
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {له ما بين أيدينا} من التقدير الأزلي

BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r3.claim: The wording resembles God's statement that He knows what is before and behind them.
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r3.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : {يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم}

BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r4.claim: God is not forgetful: He does not abandon Muhammad when revelation is delayed for wisdom, or is not inattentive.
BURSEVI:v5p266#3/r4.anchor: فعيل بمعنى فاعل من النسيان بمعنى الترك أي : تاركا لك كما زعمت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r1.claim: The words are Gabriel's answer: revelation had paused after the Prophet was asked about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; pagans said his Lord had abandoned him, and Gabriel explained he descends only when commanded. The verse and Sura al-Duha were revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r1.anchor: قال له عليه الصلاة والسلام : يا جبريل احتبست عنى حتى ساء ضنى واشتقت اليك فقالك انى كنت اشوق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r2.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r2.claim: Al-Khafaji sees this as one story linked to the preceding narrative.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r2.anchor: فهو من عطف القصة على القصة على ما قاله الخفاجي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r3.claim: After consoling the Prophet through earlier prophets and contrasting righteous successors with corrupt ones, the passage answers the pagans' claim and consoles him; angelic submission also links the passage to piety and steadfast worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r3.anchor: وفي الكشف وجه وقوع ذلك هذا الموقع أنه تعالى لم فرغ من اقاصيص الأنبياء عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r4.claim: The angel's obedience in movement and stillness prepares the command to worship and persevere, and makes the juxtaposition with the ignorant, unjust human an elegant aside.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r4.anchor: ولهذا صرح بعده بقوله تعالى ( فاعبده واصطبر لاعبادته )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r5.claim: A report in Ahmad, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and others says the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often, whereupon this verse was revealed; it may have occurred during the earlier conversation or been revealed repeatedly.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال : قال رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) لجبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام : ما يمنعك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r1.claim: Some posit an omitted introduction, this is what Gabriel said, to improve the connection, but the author says it adds no useful meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r1.anchor: أن التقدير هذاوقال جبريل : وما نتنزل الخ وبه يظهر حسن العطف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r2.speaker: النقاش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r2.claim: Al-Naqqash reports a view connecting this speech to Gabriel's earlier words, I am only a messenger of your Lord; the author deems it far from acceptable.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r2.anchor: حكى النقاش عن قوم أن الآية متصلة بقول جبريل عليه السلام أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r3.claim: التنزل normally means descending gradually, but can mean descent generally; a poetic use of تنزل does not imply gradual motion.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r3.anchor: التنزل النزول على مهل لأنه مطاوع نزل يقال نزلته فتنزل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r4.claim: The meaning is that Gabriel and the angels descend from time to time only at God's command, in accordance with His wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r4.anchor: والمعنى مانتنزل وقتا غب وقت إلا بأمر الله تعالى على ما تقتضية حكمته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r5.speaker: الأعرج
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r5.claim: Al-A'raj reads وما تنزل with a masculine verb; context and occasion identify its subject as revelation, and the speaker remains Gabriel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج ( وما تنزل ) بالياء والضمير الموحى بقرينة الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r6.claim: The standard interpretation takes what is before us as future time, behind us as past, and between as the present; angels descend in every time only by God's leave.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r6.anchor: ما قدامنا من الزمان المستقبل ( وما خلفنا ( من الزمان الماضي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj maps the three phrases to time before creation, the period after death through the hereafter, and the span of life.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جريج : ما بين الايدي هو ما مر من الزمان فبل الايجاد وما خلف هو ما بعد موتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r8.claim: Abu al-Aliya interprets them as the world until the first Trumpet, the hereafter from resurrection, and the forty years between the two blasts.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r8.anchor: وقال أبو العالية : ما بين الايدي الدنيا بأسرها إلى النفخة الأولى وما خلف ذلك الاخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r9.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس، ابن جبير، قتادة، مقاتل، سفيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r9.claim: The account in al-Tahrir wa al-Tahbir, also narrated from Ibn Abbas and others, identifies what is before as the hereafter and what is behind as the world.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r9.anchor: ورواه العوفى عن ابن عباس وبه قال ابن جبير وقتادة ومقاتل وسفيان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r10.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash takes the phrases as before creation, after extinction, and the interval between this world and the next.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r10.anchor: وقال الأخفش : ما بين الايدي هو ما قبل الخلق وما خلف هو ما بعد الفناء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r11.claim: Other views interpret the phrases spatially as sky, earth, intervening space, or destination, origin, and present location; some generalize to both space and time, all owned by God, so movement requires His permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114/r11.anchor: واختار بعضهم تفسيرها بما يعم الزمان والمكان والمراد أنه تعالى المالك لكل ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r1.speaker: البغوي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r1.claim: Al-Baghawi says the phrase means God knows all that is before, behind, and between; therefore angels do not act contrary to His wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r1.anchor: وقال البغوي : المراد له علم ما بين ايدينا الخ أي فلا نقدم على مالم يكن موافق حكمته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation generalizes the phrase to God's ownership and knowledge of everything.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r2.anchor: واختار بعضهم التعميم أي له سبحانه ذلك ملكا وعلما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r3.claim: ما كان ربك نسيا means God did not abandon His prophets, especially Muhammad; the delayed descent only means no command had been given, not that God forsook him, and this best fits the occasion.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r3.anchor: أي تارك أنبياءه عليهم السلام ويدخل ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) في ذلك دخولا أوليا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, نسيا is literal: God's encompassing knowledge and dominion exclude forgetfulness, and the delay arose from wisdom; some prefer this as the intensive form and literal wording fit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : النسيان على ظاهره يعنى أنه سبحانه لاحاطة علمه وملكه لا يطرأ عليه الغفلة والنسيان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r5.claim: The author selects the non-abandonment explanation because it better suits the reported occasion; the alternative better fits the intensive form and preserves the literal sense, though he questions that rationale.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r5.anchor: واختير الأول لأن هذا المعنى لا يجوز عليه سبحانه فلا حاجة إلى نفيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r6.claim: Repeating رب in ربك honors the Prophet, evokes his Lord's care, and signals the reason for the ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r6.anchor: وفي اعادة اسم الرب المعرب عن تبليغ إلى الكمال اللائق مضافا إلى ضميره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم، ابن بحر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r7.claim: They take the first part through وما بين ذلك as the pious speaking on entering Paradise; their descent means receiving Paradise as a home by God's command and grace, with God owning past, present, and future.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم وابن بحر : أول الآية إلى ( وما بين ذلك ) من كلام المتقين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم، ابن بحر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r8.claim: On their reading, وما كان ربك نسيا confirms that God does not forget the workers' reward or their deeds as He promised.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم وابن بحر : أول الآية إلى ( وما بين ذلك ) من كلام المتقين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r9.claim: The pious-speakers reading departs from the apparent sense, leaves ربك addressed to the Prophet unexplained, conflicts with the occasion, and seems chosen only to connect this passage to what precedes.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p114#2/r9.anchor: حمل التنزل على ما ذكر خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r1.claim: Calling God Lord of the heavens and earth explains why forgetfulness is impossible: the owner of all cannot neglect His chosen messenger; رب is either a predicate of an omitted subject or apposition to ربك.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r1.anchor: بيان لاستحالة النسيان عليه تعالى من بيده ملكوت السموات والأرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p243/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p243/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p243/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel why he did not visit, and the verse came as the answer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p243/r3.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يا جبريل ما يمنعك أن تزورنا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p243/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p243/r4.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك وقتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p243/r4.claim: They say Gabriel delayed after the Prophet promised answers about the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit without saying “if God wills”; Gabriel explained he was a commanded servant, and God also sent 93:1–3.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p243/r4.anchor: عكرمة والضحاك وقتادة ومقاتل والكلبي: احتبس جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r1.claim: They say “before us” refers to afterlife, reward, and punishment; “behind us” to past worldly life; and “between” to now through Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r1.anchor: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومقاتل: {ما بين أيدينا} من أمر الآخرة والثواب والعقاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r2.claim: Another interpretation makes “before us” the remaining world, “behind us” what has passed, and “between” the forty years between the two trumpet blasts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r2.anchor: وقيل {ما بين أيدينا} ما بقي من الدنيا {وما خلفنا} ما مضى منها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r3.claim: Another view says “between” is the span of our lives, with before and behind still meaning future and past worldly life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r3.anchor: وقيل: {ما بين أيدينا} ما بقي من الدنيا {وما خلفنا} ما مضى منها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r4.claim: Another view takes “before us” as after death, “behind us” as before creation, and “between” as the life span.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r4.anchor: وقيل: {ما بين أيدينا} بعد أن نموت {وما خلفنا} قبل أن نخلق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r5.claim: Another view says before us is the earth to which angels descend, behind us is the heaven from which they descend, and between is the air; all belong to God and angels act only by His command.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r5.anchor: وقيل: {ما بين أيدينا} الأرض إذا أردنا النزول إليها {وما خلفنا} السماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r6.claim: God is not forgetful: He has not forgotten or abandoned the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244/r6.anchor: {وما كان ربك نسيا} أي: ناسيا يقول: ما نسيك ربك أي: ما تركك

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:63-64/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:63-64/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:63-64/r2.claim: Gabriel says this to Muhammad after delayed revelation about the Cave companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; the delay was fifteen or forty days and unbelievers said God had abandoned him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:63-64/r2.anchor: حكاية قول جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام حين استبطأه رسول الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:63-64/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:63-64/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:63-64/r3.claim: Angels descend gradually or generally only by God’s wise command; all places and times belong to Him, and delayed revelation was not abandonment. Alternatively, the pious say this on entering Paradise, affirming God has not forgotten their deeds or promised reward.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:63-64/r3.anchor: لا ننتقل من مكان إلى مكان

QASHANI:19:64/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64/r1.claim: Angelic descent and the soul's connection with the higher assembly require original innate purity suited to the spiritual world and a present readiness gained through purification.
QASHANI:19:64/r1.anchor: تنزل الملائكة واتصال النفس بالملأ الأعلى إنما يكون بأمرين: استعداد أصلي وصفاء فطري يناسب به جوهر الروح العالم الأعلى، واستعداد حالي بالتصفية والتزكية

QASHANI:19:64/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64/r2.claim: Merely possessing readiness is insufficient; enduring established capacity matters, as 41:30 links descent to steadfastness.
QASHANI:19:64/r2.anchor: ولا يكفي مجرد حصولها فيه، بل المعتبر هو الملائكة: ألا ترى إلى قوله

QASHANI:19:64/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64/r3.claim: The wording about devils descending on every liar and sinner also conveys enduring capacity, so angels likewise descend only on truthful, good people.
QASHANI:19:64/r3.anchor: كيف أورد في حصول استعداد تنزلهم بناء المبالغة الدال على الملكة والدوام فكذا لا تتنزل الملائكة إلا على الصديق الخير

QASHANI:19:64/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64/r4.claim: When both kinds of readiness unite, they signal God's permission; emanation is constant, and delay comes only from absent readiness.
QASHANI:19:64/r4.anchor: وهذا الاستعداد الثاني إذا اجتمع مع الأول كان علامة إذن الحق وأمره، إذ الفيض عام، تام، غير منقطع، فحيث تأخر إنما تأخر لعدم الاستعداد

QASHANI:19:64/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64/r5.claim: Angels do not descend by their own choice but by God's choice and command.
QASHANI:19:64/r5.anchor: وما نتنزل باختيارنا بل باختياره وأمره ليس إلا

QASHANI:19:64-65/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64-65/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64-65/r1.claim: What lies ahead comprises higher, preceding stages of the World of Power that human knowledge cannot encompass.
QASHANI:19:64-65/r1.anchor: { له ما بين أيدينا } من أطوار الجبروت التي فوقنا وتتقدم أطوارنا التي وجوهنا إليها ولا يحيط علمنا بها

QASHANI:19:64-65/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64-65/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64-65/r2.claim: What lies behind comprises lower, earthly stages of the World of Dominion.
QASHANI:19:64-65/r2.anchor: { وما خلفنا } من أطوار الملكوت الأرضية التي دون أطوارنا

QASHANI:19:64-65/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64-65/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64-65/r3.claim: What lies between is the dominion's stages where we dwell; all remain under divine mastery, command, and knowledge.
QASHANI:19:64-65/r3.anchor: { وما بين ذلك } من الأطوار الملكوتية التي نحن فيها، كلهم في ملكة قهره وتحت سلطنة أمره وإحاطة علمه

QASHANI:19:64-65/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64-65/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64-65/r4.claim: God neither forgets a readiness for perfection nor withholds a due; He knows every readiness and grants its perfection once obtained, so revelation's delay lies with the recipient.
QASHANI:19:64-65/r4.anchor: { وما كان ربك نسيا } ينسى شيئا يستعد لكمال فلا يفيض عليه أو تاركا لمستحق بدون حقه بل يحيط بكل الاستعدادات علما

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r1.claim: The surah sequence answers Quraysh: al-Kahf addresses two questions, al-Isrāʾ a third, and Maryam exposes older prophetic history and religious decline after the prophets.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r1.anchor: جاءت سورة مريم كاشفة - تبكيتا لأهل الكتاب الكاتمين للحق - عن أغرب من تلك القصص زأقدم زمانا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r2.claim: This ordered response proves the Qurʾān is God’s speech: the Prophet’s reason and resolve would have let him answer the next day if he had composed it himself.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r2.anchor: ثبت بذلك أن هذا كله مرتب لإجابة سؤالهم وأنه كلام الله قطعا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r3.claim: God left the question of the Spirit open and delayed the answer for no incapacity or ignorance; accounts of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the births of Jesus and Isaac show complete power and knowledge, and the reports fit reality.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r3.anchor: ما أجمل أمر الروح ولا أخر الإجابة خمس عشرة ليلة أو أقل أو أكثر من عجز ولا جهل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r4.claim: Biqaʿi connects the verse to the Prophet telling Gabriel that he had delayed so long that the Prophet suspected him; he says similar circumstances are mentioned in revelation reports.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r4.anchor: عن قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبرئيل عليه الصلاة والسلام ( لقد أبطات علي يا جبرئيل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r5.claim: The address calls God the Prophet’s beneficent Lord to honor and reassure him, explaining that both precedence and delay occur by divine command.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r5.anchor: ووقع الخطاب مقترنا بالوصف المفهم لمزيد الإكرام تطييبا لقلبه صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r6.claim: The form tanazzul suggests honored, repeated descent at intervals; punishment instead requires command and arrives in the blink of an eye.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r6.anchor: ولفظ التنزل مشير إلى الإكرام , وهو التردد مرة بعد مرة ووقتا غب وقت

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r7.claim: Following resurrection with Paradise continues the pattern of mentioning Paradise after resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548/r7.anchor: وكان هذا عقب ذكر القيامة بذكر الجنة كما كان المعطوف عليه عقب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r1.claim: Even if the link seems distant, the verse answers objectors who might demand every account of the ancients: earlier and future reports come only by the Lord’s command.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r2.claim: What lies before and behind the angels and between it includes place, time, their own location, and what is above and below; they know and act accordingly, without acting in God’s dominion except by permission.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r2.anchor: أي من المكان والزمان وما فيهما

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r3.claim: God is never forgetful of anything, so neither the Spirit’s details nor the Prophet’s needs escaped him and no revelation delay arose from ignorance.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r3.anchor: ولا ينسى ما يصلحك فيحتاج إلى مذكر به

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r4.claim: The fifteen-night-or-more delay could look like forgetfulness to the foolish, but God continuously observes the angels and directs their work at the wise, appointed time.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r4.anchor: فكان ذلك موهما للأغبياء أنه نسيان

BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r5.claim: The intensive form nasiy denies even occasional forgetfulness: a servant could be absent without leave only if his master were prone to prolonged lapses.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p548#2/r5.anchor: أنه لا يتمكن العبد من الغيبة عن السيد بغير إذنه إلا أن كان بحيث يمكن أن يغفل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r1.claim: The next surah denies error and forgetfulness in language suited to its context, while affirming the required doctrine that God forgets nothing.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r1.anchor: فأتى في كل أسلوب بما يناسبه مع الوفاء بما يجب من حق الإعتقاد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r2.claim: Together with the Qurʾān’s truthful descent and challenge, this verse forms a guard around the answers, turning away objections from every direction.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r2.anchor: لتكون الآيات رابطة على هذه الأجوبة وتوابعها وضابطة لها كالشهب والحرس الشديد بالنسبة إلى السماء

DURR-FULL:v5p529/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r7.claim: The Prophet asks Gabriel why he visits less often; Gabriel answers that angels descend only by their Lord's command.
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبريل: ما يمنعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا

DURR-FULL:v5p529/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r8.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r8.claim: Additional transmissions say this verse was Gabriel's answer to Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r8.anchor: زاد ابن المنذر وابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم فكان ذلك الجواب لمحمد

DURR-FULL:v5p529/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r9.claim: When asked which places God loves and hates, the Prophet says he did not know until asking Gabriel; Gabriel's delay made him fear God's displeasure, and the verse answered him.
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r9.anchor: عن أنس قال: سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم - أي البقاع أحب إلى الله وأيها أبغضها إلى الله

DURR-FULL:v5p529/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r10.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r10.claim: Ikrima says Gabriel was delayed forty days; when Muhammad said he missed him, Gabriel replied that he missed Muhammad more but was commanded, then recited the verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p529/r10.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: أبطأ جبريل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعين يوما ثم نزل

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r1.claim: In Mecca Gabriel's absence grieved Muhammad, who complained to Khadija; after she suggested God had abandoned him, Gabriel came with the reassurance of 93:2 and this verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r1.anchor: عن السدي قال: احتبس جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة حتى حزن واشتد عليه

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r2.claim: Gabriel stayed away twelve nights; Muhammad told him the delay had tired him and the pagans had speculated, after which the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: لبث جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اثنتي عشرة ليلة فلما جاءه

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r3.claim: In another account, Gabriel explains that angels were held back because the people they visited neglected nail trimming, cleaning knuckles, trimming moustaches, and using the tooth-stick.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: أبطأت الرسل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أتاه جبريل فقال: ما حبسك عني

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r4.claim: He interprets what lies before the angels as the world and what lies behind them as the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: احتبس جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فوجد رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r5.claim: He glosses what is before as the world and what is behind as the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة {له ما بين أيدينا} قال: الدنيا {وما خلفنا} قال: الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r6.claim: He reverses that interpretation: what lies before is the Hereafter, what behind is the world, and what is between them is the interval between the two.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه {له ما بين أيدينا} قال: من أمر الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r7.claim: He glosses what lies between as the interval between the two trumpet blasts.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {وما بين ذلك} قال: ما بين النفختين

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r8.claim: He also says the interval between them is between the trumpet blasts.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r8.anchor: عن أبي العالية {وما بين ذلك} قال: ما بين النفختين

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r9.claim: God's being forgetful means He will not forget Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r9.anchor: عن السدي {وما كان ربك نسيا} قال: {وما كان ربك} لينساك يا محمد

DURR-FULL:v5p530/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r10.claim: The Prophet says what God made lawful or forbidden in scripture is so, while what He left unmentioned is pardon to accept; God did not forget anything.
DURR-FULL:v5p530/r10.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء رفع الحديث قال: ما أحل الله في كتابه فهو حلال وما حرم فهو حرام

DURR-FULL:v5p531/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r1.claim: A report through Jabir repeats that what God left unmentioned is pardoned and that He does not forget.
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r1.anchor: ثم تلا {وما كان ربك نسيا} وأخرج ابن مردويه من حديث جابر مثله

DURR-FULL:v5p531/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r2.claim: Asked about clarified butter, cheese, and fur, the Prophet says lawful is what God made lawful in scripture, forbidden is what He forbade, and silence is pardon.
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r2.anchor: عن سلمان سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن السمن والجبن [] والفراء فقال: الحلال ما أحل الله في كتابه

QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r14.claim: Angels descend only by God's command, to aid the oppressed, rescue the distressed, destroy deniers, support believers, and attend countless other matters.
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r14.anchor: فبعضهم بإنجاد المظلومين ، وبعضهم بإغاثة الملهوفين

QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r15.claim: God does not neglect either rejector or worshipper: He preserves and blesses, or grants respite and punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r15.anchor: والله - سبحانه - لا يترك جاحدا ولا عابدا من حفظ وإنعام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the verse’s placement unusual but accepts the report from Ibn ʿAbbās as its most reliable and fitting occasion of revelation: Gabriel delayed, and the Prophet asked him to visit more often.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r1.anchor: فقال جمهور المفسرين : إن سبب نزولها أن جبريل عليه السلام أبطأ أياما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r2.claim: The report transmitted by al-Bukhārī and al-Tirmidhī says the Prophet asked Gabriel to visit more often after Gabriel’s delayed visits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r2.anchor: رواه البخاري والترمذي عن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r3.claim: God commands Gabriel to say the verse as an answer to the Prophet; an implicit “say” is omitted, and the verse was fixed where revelation had reached after the preceding prophetic stories.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r3.anchor: أن الله أمر جبريل عليه السلام أن يقول هذا الكلام جوابا عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r4.claim: The Prophet’s question came at the end of the prophetic stories; the verse entered the Qur’an at the point revelation had reached.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r4.anchor: ولا شك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ذلك لجبريل عليه السلام عند انتهاء قصص الأنبياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r5.claim: The pronoun refers to Gabriel and the angels: they descend and meet messengers only at God’s command, never by their own choice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r5.anchor: أعلم الله نبيئه على لسان جبريل أن نزول الملائكة لا يقع إلا عن أمر الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r6.claim: Tanazzul means descend; its form suggests exertion because angels’ descent from their realm is unusual, as also in the Night of Decree verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r6.anchor: مرادف ننزل ، وأصل التنزل : تكلف النزول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r7.claim: The lām in lahu marks ownership of governance; before, behind, and between cover the front, back, right, and left, encompassing directions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p139/r7.anchor: واللام في ( له ) للملك ، وهو ملك التصرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r1.claim: Because the spatial regions belong to God, they stand metonymically for their contents; the expression encompasses all beings, their states and actions, and past, present, and future times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r1.anchor: ولما كان ذلك مخبرا عنه بأنه ملك لله تعين أن يراد به الكائنات التي في تلك الجهات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r2.claim: If the verse answers the Prophet through Gabriel, “not forgetful” can mean God does not abandon him; the intensified form can emphasize the long interval before resuming revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r2.anchor: بتارك ، أي ما كان ربك تاركك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r3.claim: Alternatively, nasiya is an intensive negation of forgetfulness, affirming God’s comprehensive knowledge: angels descend only when His knowledge and wisdom call for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r3.anchor: فيتعين صرف المبالغة إلى جانب نسبة نفي النسيان عن الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم وصاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r4.claim: Abū Muslim and al-Kashshāf allow the verse to continue the speech of Paradise’s inhabitants: they descend there only by their Lord’s command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r4.anchor: أن هذه الآية من تمام حكاية كلام أهل الجنة بتقدير فعل يقولون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r5.claim: On that alternative, the address “your Lord” is one speaker addressing another; “your Lord was not forgetful” may be God’s coda to the Prophet or the people of Paradise affirming their Lord kept His promise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p140/r5.anchor: من قول الله تعالى لرسوله تذييلا لما قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r1.claim: The majority read natanazzalu with nūn, as Gabriel speaks for himself and the angels; al-Aʿraj reads yatanazzalu with yāʾ, which some take as God's statement that Gabriel does not descend.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r1.anchor: قرأ الجمهور «وما نتنزل» بالنون كأن جبريل عنى نفسه والملائكة، وقرأ الأعرج وما «يتنزل» بالياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r2.claim: The interpretation of the yāʾ reading as God's report does not fit “what is before us”; it better reads as Gabriel saying revelation descends only at God's appointed times.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r2.anchor: ويرده قوله ما بين أيدينا لأنه لا يطرد معه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r3.speaker: الأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r3.claim: A second report gives al-Aʿraj's form with ḍamma on the yāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masud reads “except by your Lord's word.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r4.anchor: ورويت قراءة الأعرج بضم الياء، وقرأ ابن مسعود «إلا بقول ربك» ،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say the verse came when Gabriel once arrived late and the Prophet asked him to visit more often.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: سبب هذه الآية، أن النبي عليه السلام أبطأ عنه جبريل مرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r6.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak connect the verse to Gabriel's delay in answering the Cave questions, after the Prophet said he would answer the next day; it resembles Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك: سببها أن جبريل تأخر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند قوله في السؤالات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r7.claim: The wāw links one statement to another even though their meanings differ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r7.anchor: وهذه الواو التي في قوله وما نتنزل هي عاطفة جملة كلام على أخرى وواصلة بين القولين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r8.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r8.claim: Al-Naqqash reports a weak view that the verse continues Jesus' statement at 19:19, “I am only your Lord's messenger.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r8.anchor: وحكى النقاش عن قوم أن قوله وما نتنزل متصل بقوله إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك غلاما زكيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r9.claim: Abu al-Aliyya maps “before us” to worldly life until the first trumpet, “behind” to the afterlife from resurrection, and “between” to the interval between trumpet blasts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r9.anchor: فقال أبو العالية «ما بين الأيدي» في الدنيا بأسرها إلى النفخة الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p23#2/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj says “before us” is time before creation, “behind us” runs from death into everlasting life, and “between” is the span of earthly life.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r1.claim: The verse stresses that angels belong to God and act or move only by His command and wisdom; the places belong to Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r1.anchor: والآية إنما المقصد بها الإشعار بملك الله تعالى لملائكة وأن قليل تصرفهم وكثيرة إنما هو بأمره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r2.claim: Alternatively, “before” and “behind” refer to angels' workspaces and “between” to the angels and their stations: they cannot move except by God's power and command.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r2.anchor: فلو ذهب بالآية إلى أن المراد ب «ما بين الأيدي وما خلف» الأمكنة التي فيها تصرفهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r3.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas and Qatada reverses the usual temporal sense, making “before” the afterlife and “behind” this world; Ibn Atiyya finds it incoherent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة فيما روي وما أراه صحيحا عنهما «ما بين الأيدي هي الآخرة وما خلف هو الدنيا» ،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r4.claim: The temporal reading of Abu al-Aliyya works for people, not angels; “before” normally means what preceded in time, as Torah and Gospel preceded the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r4.anchor: وهذا مختل المعنى إلا على التشبيه بالمكان لأن ما بين اليد إنما هو ما تقدم وجوده في الزمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r5.claim: God's not being forgetful means He has not forgotten to send the angels; their coming is delayed to the proper time. The implications differ by occasion-of-revelation account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r5.anchor: وقوله وما كان ربك نسيا أي ممن يلحقه نسيان بعثنا إليكم في وقت المصلحة به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r6.claim: Under one account, the delay tells Muhammad not to seek Gabriel's visits more often than God wills; under the other, not to fret over delay or disbelievers' delight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r6.anchor: فلا تطلب أنت يا محمد الزيارة أكثر مما شاء الله هذا ما تقتضيه قوة الكلام على التأويل الواحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r7.claim: Nasiyyan denotes forgetfulness or heedlessness; interpreting it as “one who abandons” is weak because God's non-forgetfulness is absolute, while abandonment is not.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة نسيا هنا معناه تاركا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r8.claim: The Qur'an uses taraka (“left/abandoned”) of God in other contexts, so the unqualified denial here should remain “forgetful.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r8.anchor: ألا ترى قوله تعالى: وتركهم في ظلمات [البقرة: 17] وقوله وتركنا بعضهم يومئذ يموج في بعض [الكهف: 99]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r9.claim: Ibn Masud reads “and what is between that, and your Lord has not forgotten you.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «وما بين ذلك وما نسيك ربك» ،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r10.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r10.claim: Abu al-Darda transmits a Prophetic saying that what God made lawful or forbidden in scripture is such, while what He left unaddressed is pardon; the Prophet then recited this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r10.anchor: وروى أبو الدرداء أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ما أحل الله في كتابه فهو حلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r1.speaker: ابن السميفع وابن يعمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r1.claim: These readers use the verb with an open yāʾ: وما يتنزل.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع وابن يعمر وما يتنزل بياء مفتوحة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r2.claim: One occasion report says the Prophet asked Gabriel why he did not visit more often, and this verse was revealed; Saʿid ibn Jubayr transmits it from Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يا جبريل ما يمنعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says an angel delayed, then cited the community's failure to clean teeth, trim nails, and clean finger joints; the verse was revealed. Al-Anbari defines the knuckle folds and the spaces between them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r3.anchor: قاله مجاهد قال ابن الأنباري البراجم عند العرب الفصوص التي في فصول ظهور الأصابع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r4.claim: They say Gabriel was delayed when the Prophet was asked about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; he explained that he was a commanded servant, descending when sent and holding back when held back.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r4.anchor: قاله عكرمة وقتادة والضحاك وفي سبب احتباس جبريل عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r5.claim: Two explanations are given for Gabriel's detention: the community's lack of full cleanliness, or the Prophet's promise to answer about the Cave Companions the next day without saying “if God wills.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما لامتناع أصحابه من كمال النظافة كما ذكرنا في حديث مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r6.claim: The delay is variously said to be fifteen days (Ibn ʿAbbās), forty days (ʿIkrima and Maqātil), twelve nights (Mujahid), three days (Maqātil), or twenty-five days (al-Thaʿlabi).
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r6.anchor: أحدها خمسة عشر يوما وقد ذكرناه في الكهف عن ابن عباس والثاني أربعون يوما قاله عكرمة ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r7.claim: Some say Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā was revealed over this delay; the majority understand the speaker here to be Gabriel, though al-Mawardi reports an alternative about Paradise's inhabitants descending only by God's command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p248#2/r7.anchor: وقيل إن سورة الضحى نزلت في هذا السبب والمفسرون على أن قوله وما نتنزل الا بأمر ربك قول جبريل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r1.claim: One view says what is before the angels is the afterlife and what is behind them is this world; Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and Maqātil agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r1.anchor: ما بين أيدينا الآخرة وما خلفنا الدنيا رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس وبه قال سعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r2.claim: Mujahid gives the reverse: what is before them is what has passed of the world and what is behind them is the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r2.anchor: ما بين أيدينا ما مضى من الدنيا وما خلفنا من الآخرة فهو عكس الاول قاله مجهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r3.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash says what is before them is before their creation and what is behind them comes after their extinction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r3.anchor: وقال الأخفش ما بين أيدينا قبل ان نخلق وما خلفتا بعد الفناء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r4.claim: One explanation of “what is between those” is the span between the world and the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r4.anchor: أحدها ما بين الدنيا والآخرة قاله سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r5.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة وأبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r5.claim: Another explanation is the period between the two trumpet blasts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r5.anchor: والثاني ما بين النفختين قاله مجاهد وعكرمة وأبو العالية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r6.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r6.claim: A third explanation is the time when the angels exist.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r7.claim: The singular demonstrative can refer to two things because Arabic uses a singular reference for duals and plurals.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r7.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري وإنما وحد ذلك والإشارة إلى شيئين أحدهما ما بين أيدينا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r9.claim: The statement means God did not abandon the Prophet when revelation was delayed; Muqatil similarly says God did not forget him during the interruption.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r9.anchor: ما كان تاركا لك منذ أبطأ الوحي عنك قاله ابن عباس قال مقاتل ما نسيك عند انقطاع الوحي عنك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God knows what was and what will be and forgets nothing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p250/r10.anchor: أنه عالم بما كان ويكون لا ينسى شيئا قاله الزجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often, and this verse was revealed as the answer; al-Bukhari includes this report in his tafsir and related versions add that it answered Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبريل:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r2.claim: Al-ʿAwfi's account says Gabriel had been delayed, leaving the Prophet saddened, then explained that he descends only by his Lord's command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r2.anchor: وقال العوفي عن ابن عباس: احتبس جبريل عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فوجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من ذلك وحزن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says Gabriel was absent twelve nights; on return the Prophet said the delay had distressed him and prompted the polytheists' suspicions, and the verse resembles al-Duha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لبث جبريل عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم اثنتي عشرة ليلة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak, Qatada, al-Suddi, and others likewise connect the revelation to Gabriel's delayed arrival.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r4.anchor: وكذلك قال الضحاك بن مزاحم، وقتادة، والسدي، وغير واحد: إنها نزلت في احتباس جبريل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r5.claim: ʿIkrima reports a forty-day delay and a conversation in which Gabriel says he was eager to visit but was under orders; Ibn Kathir calls the report unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: أبطأ جبريل النزول على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعين يوما، ثم نزل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r6.claim: A report from Mujahid says Gabriel cited neglected grooming practices as the reason for delayed visits, then recited this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p248#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: أبطأت الرسل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، ثم أتاه جبريل فقال له: ما حبسك يا جبريل؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249/r1.claim: A prophetic report from Ibn ʿAbbas attributes Gabriel's delay to the community not using the tooth-stick, trimming nails and moustaches, or cleaning between fingers; Ahmad transmits a similar report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أن جبريل أبطأ عليه، فذكر ذلك له فقال: وكيف وأنتم لا تستنون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249/r2.speaker: أم سلمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249/r2.claim: Umm Salama says the Prophet asked her to prepare the sitting place because an angel was about to descend to earth, having never descended there before.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249/r2.anchor: عن أم سلمة قالت: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أصلحي لنا المجلس، فإنه ينزل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r1.speaker: أبو العالية وعكرمة ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة والسدي والربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r1.claim: One interpretation takes what is before the angels as worldly affairs, what is behind as the afterlife, and what lies between as the interval between the two Trumpet blasts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r1.anchor: قيل: المراد ما بين أيدينا: أمر الدنيا، وما خلفنا: أمر الآخرة، {وما بين ذلك} ما بين النفختين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك وقتادة وابن جريج والثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r2.claim: A second view takes what is before as the coming afterlife, what is behind as past worldly affairs, and what lies between as the span between them; Ibn Jarir prefers it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: {ما بين أيدينا} ما نستقبل من أمر الآخرة، {وما خلفنا} أي: ما مضى من الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi explain that the Lord was not forgetful as meaning He had not forgotten the Prophet, paralleling al-Duha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: {وما كان ربك نسيا} قال مجاهد [والسدي] (1) معناه: ما نسيك ربك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r4.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says what God makes lawful or forbidden is so, while what He leaves unmentioned is pardon; God would not forget anything, and the Prophet recites this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p249#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء يرفعه قال: "ما أحل الله في كتابه فهو حلال وما حرم فهو حرام وما سكت

AKHFASH:v2p438#2/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p438#2/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p438#2/r6.claim: ما بين أيدينا means before creation, ما خلفنا after extinction, and ما بين ذلك the period while the angels existed.
AKHFASH:v2p438#2/r6.anchor: وقال {له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما [150 ء] بين ذالك} يقول {ما بين أيدينا} قبل ان نخلق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r1.claim: The words are Gabriel's explanation for his delayed descent when the Prophet was waiting for him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r1.anchor: حكاية قول جبريل صلوات الله عليه حين استبطأه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r2.claim: A report says Gabriel was detained forty days; another says fifteen, after questions about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r2.anchor: أنه احتبس أربعين يوما . وقيل : خمسة عشر يوما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r3.claim: The polytheists said the Prophet's Lord had abandoned and detested him; the verse and Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā then came down.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r4.claim: The Prophet said Gabriel's delay distressed him and that he missed him; Gabriel replied that he too longed for him but was only commanded, descending when sent and waiting when detained.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r4.anchor: أبطأت حتى ساء ظني واشتقت إليك . قال : إني كنت أشوق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r5.claim: Tanazzul can mean gradual descent or descent generally; a cited poem supports the sense of descending from the sky, and gradual descent best fits here.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r6.claim: The angels descend only at intervals when God commands, as He judges wise and prudent.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r6.anchor: في الأحايين وقتاغب وقت ليس إلا بأمر الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r7.claim: What is before, behind, and between the angels means all directions and places; they cannot move from one place to another without the King's command.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r7.anchor: من الجهات والأماكن { وما بين ذالك } وما نحن فيها فلا نتمالك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r8.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r8.claim: The phrases may denote past worldly affairs, future afterlife affairs, and the forty-year interval between the two trumpet blasts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r8.anchor: ما سلف من أمر الدنيا وما يستقبل من أمر الآخرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r9.claim: Other glosses are elapsed and remaining lifetimes with the present state, what precedes existence and follows extinction, or earth, heaven, and what lies between.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r9.anchor: ما مضى من أعمارنا وما غبر منها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r10.claim: All the glosses express God's encompassing knowledge: nothing is hidden from Him, so angelic action must follow His wisdom, command, and permission.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r10.anchor: المحيط بكل شيء لا تخفى عليه خافية ولا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r11.claim: “Your Lord was not forgetful” means He did not abandon the Prophet; the delay awaited what was wise, as in the verse of al-Ḍuḥā.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r11.anchor: وما كان تاركا لك ، كقوله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r12.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, these are the pious speaking on entering Paradise: they enter only by God's grace for their deeds, and He has not forgotten their recompense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r12.anchor: هي حكاية قول المتقين حين يدخلون الجنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r13.claim: On that alternative, God confirms that He does not forget workers' deeds, then the Prophet is told to worship and work so God may reward him like the pious.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r13.anchor: فحين عرفته على هذه الصفة ، فأقبل على العمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r14.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads يتنزل with yāʾ, relating the report to Gabriel, with the pronoun referring to revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r14.anchor: بالياء على الحكاية عن جبريل عليه السلام والضمير للوحي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r15.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads إلا بقول ربك; the vocalic disagreement in النسي should match that in البغي.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r15.anchor: يجب أن يكون الخلاف في النسي مثله في البغي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r3.claim: With that parsing, “your Lord was not forgetful” may be the pious speaking, while the following words are God's speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r3.anchor: وما بعده من كلام رب العزة

FARRA:v2p170/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p170/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p170/r3.claim: The ones who descend are the angels; ‘before us’ concerns worldly affairs, ‘behind us’ the afterlife, and ‘between that’ the interval between trumpet blasts.
FARRA:v2p170/r3.anchor: وقوله: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك [64] يعني الملائكة وقوله: له (ما بين أيدينا) من أمر الدنيا (وما خلفنا) من أمر الآخرة

FARRA:v2p170/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p170/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p170/r4.claim: One interpretation of ‘what is between that’ is the forty-year interval between the two trumpet blasts.
FARRA:v2p170/r4.anchor: وما بين ذلك) يقال ما بين النفختين، وبينهما أربعون سنة.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r1.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r1.claim: The words may be spoken by Paradise's inhabitants, who descend only to places God commands.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r1.anchor: أنه قول أهل الجنة : إننا لا ننزل موضعا من الجنة إلا بأمر الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r2.claim: Alternatively, Gabriel says this after delaying twelve nights; on his return the Prophet said the pagans had made every sort of claim during his absence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r2.anchor: أنه قول جبريل عليه السلام , لما ذكر أن جبريل أبطأ على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم باثنتي عشرة ليلة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r3.claim: The descent may occur when God commands the angels to descend, or when God commands Gabriel to bring revelation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r3.anchor: إذا أمرنا نزلنا عليك . الثاني : إذا أمرك ربك نزلنا عليك الأمر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r4.claim: What is before means the afterlife, what is behind this world, and what is between them the interval between trumpet blasts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r4.anchor: { ما بين أيدينا } من الآخرة , { وما خلفنا } من الدنيا . { وما بين ذلك } يعني ما بين النفختين

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r5.claim: Another reading takes before as past worldly life, behind as what follows in this world and the hereafter, and between as all that preceded and follows.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r5.anchor: { ما بين أيدينا } أي ما مضى أمامنا من الدنيا , { وما خلفنا } ما يكون بعدنا من الدنيا والآخرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r6.claim: A third possibility is that before is heaven, behind earth, and between is the space between them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r6.anchor: { ما بين أيدينا } : السماء , { وما خلفنا } : الأرض . { وما بين ذلك } ما بين السماء والأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r7.claim: God is not forgetful either means He has not forgotten you or does not possess forgetfulness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r7.anchor: أي ما نسيك ربك . الثاني : وما كان ربك ذا نسيان

MUJAHID:v1p387#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p387#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p387#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says the angels spoke this when the Prophet asked them to visit, linking it with 'Your Lord has not forsaken you nor detested you.'
MUJAHID:v1p387#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك ﴾ قال هذا قول الملائكة

MUQATIL:19:61-65/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:61-65/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:61-65/r5.claim: Gabriel was delayed from the Prophet for forty days, or, in another account, three days; Meccan polytheists said his Lord had abandoned and hated him. When Gabriel came, each expressed longing for the other.
MUQATIL:19:61-65/r5.anchor: أن جبريل، عليه السلام، احتبس على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعين يوما، ويقال: ثلاثة أيام

MUQATIL:19:61-65/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:61-65/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:61-65/r6.claim: Gabriel descends only by God's command; God's authority covers the Hereafter, the world, and what lies between them, including the interval between the two blasts. This answers the claim that God forgot the Prophet.
MUQATIL:19:61-65/r6.anchor: { له ما بين أيدينا } من أمر الآخرة، { وما خلفنا } من أمر الدنيا، { وما بين ذلك } ، يعني ما بين الدنيا والآخرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often, and this verse then descended.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي عليه السلام قال يا جبريل ما منعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا فنزل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r2.claim: Tanazzul can mean descending gradually or descent in general; the first sense suits Gabriel's arrival from time to time only by God's command.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r2.anchor: والتنزل على معنيين معنى النزول على مهل ومعنى النزول على الاطلاق والأول أليق هنا يعني ان نزولنا في الاحايين وقتا غب وقت ليس إلا بأمر الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r3.claim: God owns the angels' locations in front, behind, and between them, so they cannot move from place to place without His will and command.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r3.anchor: أي له ما قدامنا وما خلفنا من الأماكن وما نحن فيها فلا نتمالك أن ننتقل من مكان إلى مكان إلا بأمر الله ومشيئته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r4.claim: God knows and preserves every motion, stillness, and change; forgetfulness cannot be attributed to Him, and angels move only with permission.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#3/r4.anchor: وهو الحافظ العالم بكل حركة وسكون وما يحدث من الأحوال لا تجوز عليه الغفلة والنسيان فأنى لنا أن نتقلب في ملكوته إلا إذا أذن لنا فيه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#10/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#10/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#10/r1.claim: The statement that the angels descend only by their Lord's command may be spoken by the angels or by Gabriel.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#10/r1.anchor: {وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك} قول الملائكة، أو قول جبريل صلى الله عليه.
