QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r1.claim: A Tirmidhi report says the verse answered Muhammad's question to Gabriel about why he visited less; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan gharib.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r1.anchor:
روى الترمذي عن ابن عباس قال:
" قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبريل: «ما منعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا» قال: فنزلت هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r2.claim: Bukhari transmits the same exchange and says this revelation was Gabriel's answer to Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r2.anchor: ورواه البخاري: حدثنا خلاد بن يحيى حدثنا عمر بن ذر قال: سمعت أبي يحدث عن سعيد بن جبير

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r3.claim: Mujahid says an angel explained his delay by pointing to people's neglected grooming: uncut nails and mustaches, unclean finger joints, and lack of tooth-cleaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: " أبطأ الملك على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أتاه، فقال: «ما الذي أبطأك»

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r4.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وعكرمة والضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r4.claim: They say Gabriel withheld himself while Muhammad awaited answers about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; reports give delays of forty days, twelve nights, fifteen, thirteen, or three days.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا وقتادة وعكرمة والضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي: احتبس جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين سأله قومه عن قصة أصحاب الكهف وذي القرنين والروح

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r5.speaker: جبريل
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r5.claim: Gabriel says he longed for Muhammad too but descends only when sent and stays away when held back; the passage is linked to the opening of al-Duha.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r5.anchor: قال جبريل عليه السلام: إني كنت أشوق، ولكني عبد مأمور إذا بعثت نزلت، وإذا حبست احتبست

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r6.claim: An alternative says Paradise's inhabitants speak these words on entering their gardens; on that reading this passage continues the preceding description.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو إخبار من أهل الجنة أنهم يقولون عند دخولها: وما نتنزل هذه الجنان إلا بأمر ربك.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r7.claim: The words may be a divine instruction to Gabriel: either angels descend when ordered or only when the Lord orders, with the command aimed at descent in one reading and revelation-sending in the other.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r7.anchor: «وما نتنزل» أي قال الله تعالى: قل يا جبريل { وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك }. وهذا يحتمل وجهين

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r8.claim: Lahu means to God; what lies before, behind, and between the angels is God's knowledge and domain.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r8.anchor: وقوله تعالى: { له } أي لله. { ما بين أيدينا } أي علم ما بين أيدينا { وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك }

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r9.claim: They interpret before as past worldly affairs, behind as future worldly events and the afterlife, and between as the intermediate state.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس وابن جريج: ما مضى أمامنا من أمر الدنيا، وما يكون بعدنا من أمرها وأمر الآخرة «وما بين ذلك» البرزخ.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r1.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r1.claim: They say what is ahead is the afterlife, behind is the past world, and between is the forty-year interval between the blasts.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r1.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل: «له ما بين أيدينا» من أمر الآخرة «وما خلفنا» ما مضى من الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash says before us means before creation, behind us after death, and between them life from creation to death.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r2.anchor: الأخفش: «ما بين أيدينا» ما كان قبل أن نخلق «وما خلفنا» ما يكون بعد أن نموت

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes before as afterlife reward and punishment, behind as past deeds, and between as the present until Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: «ما بين أيدينا» من الثواب والعقاب وأمور الآخرة. «وما خلفنا» ما مضى من أعمالنا في الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r4.claim: One possibility maps what is ahead to heaven, behind to earth, and between to the space separating them.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r4.anchor: ويحتمل خامسا: «ما بين أيدينا» السماء «وما خلفنا» الأرض «وما بين ذلك» أي ما بين السماء والأرض.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r5.claim: A variant attributed to Ibn Abbas reverses the map: before us is the world down to earth, behind us the heavens, and between us the air.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية: «له ما بين أيدينا» يريد الدنيا إلى الأرض «وما خلفنا» يريد السموات

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says this can mean elapsed and remaining lifespans plus the present; the singular demonstrative refers to all the preceding items.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r6.anchor: الزمخشري: وقيل ما مضى من أعمارنا وما غبر منها، والحال التي نحن فيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r7.claim: God is never forgetful means He sends revelation when He wills, has not forgotten the Prophet despite a delay, or knows all things without forgetting them.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r7.anchor: { وما كان ربك نسيا } أي ناسيا إذا شاء أن يرسل إليك أرسل. وقيل: المعنى لم ينسك وإن تأخر عنك الوحي.

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r1.claim: A stylistic objection asks why the angels’ words are coordinated with God’s speech in the preceding verse without a separator; a clear contextual cue makes this acceptable.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r1.anchor: في الآية إشكالا وهو أو قوله : { تلك الجنة التى نورث من عبادنا من كان تقيا

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r2.claim: The author answers that clear contextual clues allow such coordination, as in the transition from God’s speech to Jesus’ words in the cited verses.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r2.anchor: أنه إذا كانت القرينة ظاهرة لم يقبح كما أن قوله سبحانه : { إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r3.claim: The apparent speaker is a group addressing one person, fitting the angels who descend to the Messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك } خطاب جماعة لواحد وذلك لا يليق إلا بالملائكة الذين ينزلون على

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r4.claim: A reported occasion says Quraysh sent five men to the Jews, who advised asking Muhammad about the youths of the Cave, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; he promised an answer without saying God willing, and revelation was delayed for forty or fifteen days.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r4.anchor: فاحتبس الوحي عنه أربعين يوما وقيل خمسة عشر يوما فشق عليه ذلك مشقة شديدة

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r5.claim: The delay distressed Muhammad, and the polytheists said his Lord had abandoned or hated him; Gabriel explained that he descends only when sent and stays back when held back.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r5.anchor: وقال المشركون ودعه ربه وقلاه ، فنزل جبريل عليه السلام فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبطأت عني

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r6.claim: This account connects the verse with the command not to promise a future act without God’s will and with the revelation of al-Duha.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r6.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية وأنزل قوله : { ولا تقولن لشىء إنى فاعل

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r7.claim: The angels’ “what is before us, behind us, and between” may mean every time—past, future, and present—or this world, the Hereafter, and what lies between.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r7.anchor: أي هو المدبر لنا في كل الأوقات الماضي والمستقبل وما بينهما أو الدنيا والآخرة وما بينهما

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r8.claim: These phrases emphasize that God manages angels and all affairs through His will, wisdom, and command, with no one entitled to object.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r8.anchor: والغرض أن أمرنا موكول إلى الله تعالى يتصرف فينا بحسب مشيئته وإرادته وحكمته لا اعتراض لأحد عليه فيه

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r9.claim: Abu Muslim proposes that Paradise’s inhabitants speak: they descend to Paradise only by God’s command; before them is their future in Paradise, behind them their worldly past, and between the two the intervening period.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r9.anchor: يجوز أن يكون قول أهل الجنة والمراد وما نتنزل الجنة إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا أي في الجنة مستقبلا

RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r10.claim: On Abu Muslim’s reading, “your Lord is never forgetful” begins God’s address to the Messenger and assures that resurrection will not be forgotten.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204/r10.anchor: وما كان ربك نسيا لشيء مما خلق فيترك إعادته لأنه عالم الغيب لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة

RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says tanazzul means either descending gradually or descent generally; the gradual sense fits repeated angelic descents over time.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r1.anchor: التنزل على معنيين : أحدهما : النزول على مهل . والثاني : بمعنى النزول على الإطلاق

RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r2.claim: The author prefers the gradual sense: angels descend at intervals only when God commands.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r2.anchor: واللائق بمثل هذا الموضع هو النزول على مهل والمراد أن نزولنا في الأحايين وقتا بعد وقت ليس إلا بأمر الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r3.claim: “Before us, behind us, and between” can mean all directions and the angels’ current place; they cannot move between heaven and earth except by God’s order.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r3.anchor: له ما قدامنا وما خلفنا من الجهات وما نحن فيه فلا نتمالك أن ننتقل من جهة إلى جهة

RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r4.claim: A second reading assigns the phrases to worldly events past, future events of the Hereafter, and the forty years between the two trumpet blasts.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r4.anchor: ما سلف من أمر الدنيا وما خلفنا ما يستقبل من أمر الآخرة وما بين ذلك وما بين النفختين وهو أربعون سنة

RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r5.claim: Other readings are past and remaining lifespan with the present, or the period before existence and after annihilation.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r5.anchor: ما مضى من أعمارنا وما غبر من ذلك والحال التي نحن فيها . ورابعها : ما قبل وجودنا وما بعد

RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r6.claim: Another reading locates the phrases in the terrain: earth before the descending angels, heaven behind them, and the space between.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r6.anchor: الأرض التي بين أيدينا إذا نزلنا والسماء التي وراءنا وما بين السماء والأرض

RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r7.claim: Every interpretation conveys that God encompasses all things and nothing is hidden from Him; angels therefore act only by His command and judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v21p204#2/r7.anchor: فالمقصود أنه المحيط بكل شيء لا تخفى عليه خافية ولا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة فكيف نقدم على فعل إلا بأمره وحكمه

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r1.claim: “Your Lord is not forgetful” means God has not abandoned Muhammad, as al-Duha says He neither forsook nor hated him; revelation paused because no command to descend had been given.
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r1.anchor: أي تاركا لك كقوله : { ما * وعدك * ربك وما قلى

STUDYQURAN:19:64/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r1.claim: The verse reportedly followed a revelation hiatus of twelve, fifteen, or forty nights, when the Prophet was asked about the Cave's people, Dhu’l-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; the delay troubled him and idolaters said God had abandoned him.
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r1.anchor: there had been an unusually long period—reportedly twelve, fifteen, or forty nights

STUDYQURAN:19:64/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r2.claim: After Gabriel returned, the Prophet reportedly asked why he did not visit more often; the verse gives Gabriel's response, and its opening We refers to the archangel.
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r2.anchor: The present verse is understood to represent Gabriel’s direct response to the Prophet’s question

STUDYQURAN:19:64/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r3.speaker: minority interpretation
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r3.claim: A minority reads the speaker as the people of Paradise, who settle there only by God's command.
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r3.anchor: A minority interpretation understands this verse to convey the words of the people of the Garden

STUDYQURAN:19:64/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r4.claim: Before and behind may refer to temporal periods—world and Hereafter, before creation and after annihilation, or past and future—or spatially to earth and Heaven; what lies between may be the two trumpet blasts or earthly life, showing God's command of all time and space.
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r4.anchor: God’s possession of these three temporal or spatial dimensions indicates His encompassing all time and space

STUDYQURAN:19:64/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r5.claim: Not forgetful reassures the Prophet that God has not forgotten him; revelation's intervals are providential and ultimately beneficial.
STUDYQURAN:19:64/r5.anchor: any interval between the revelations is providential and for his ultimate benefit

NAHHAS:v3p21/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p21/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p21/r12.claim: ما بين أيدينا means before creation, ما خلفنا what comes after death, and ما بين ذلك the period since creation.
NAHHAS:v3p21/r12.anchor: أي قبل أن نخلق ( وما خلفنا ) ما يكون بعد الموت

TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r1.claim: The verse was revealed because the Prophet felt Gabriel was slow in bringing revelation.
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r1.anchor: ما يمنعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا

TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Muhammad asked Gabriel why he did not visit more often, and this verse came as the answer.
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، أن محمدا، قال لجبرائيل: «ما يمنعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا» فنزلت هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r3.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbas report says Gabriel had been withheld, leaving the Prophet sad, then came and recited the verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله {وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك} [مريم: 64] . . إلى {وما كان ربك نسيا} [مريم: 64] قال: احتبس جبرائيل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r4.claim: Qatada says Gabriel had stayed away and the Prophet felt the delay; when Gabriel arrived, he recited the verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: لبث جبرائيل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فكأن النبي استبطأه

TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r5.claim: In another account, Gabriel paused during some revelation; the Prophet said he had longed for him, and Gabriel answered with the verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p578#3/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا} [مريم: 64] قال: هذا قول جبرائيل، احتبس جبرائيل في بعض الوحي

TAB-FULL:v15p582/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r1.claim: Mujahid takes this as the angels’ reply when Muhammad thought their descent delayed, comparing it with a passage in Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā.
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله تبارك وتعالى {وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك} [مريم: 64] قال: قول الملائكة حين استراثهم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، كالتي في الضحى

TAB-FULL:v15p582/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r2.claim: Mujahid reports Gabriel was absent from Muhammad for twelve nights; when he returned, Muhammad said the delay had made the polytheists suspect everything, and this verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، قال: لبث جبرائيل عن محمد، اثنتي عشرة ليلة

TAB-FULL:v15p582/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Gabriel was withheld until the polytheists talked about it and the Prophet became distressed; Gabriel explained he is only a servant who obeys God’s command.
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك} [مريم: 64] احتبس عن نبي الله

TAB-FULL:v15p582/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ interprets what is before the angels as this world, what is behind as the afterlife, and what lies between as the interval between the trumpet blasts.
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، {له ما بين أيدينا} [مريم: 64] يعني الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v15p582/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r5.claim: Abu al-ʿĀliya gives the same mapping: this world ahead, the afterlife behind, and the interval between the blasts in between.
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية، قال {ما بين أيدينا} [مريم: 64] من الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v15p582/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r6.claim: Another view reverses the first two terms: the afterlife is before them and this world behind them, with the intervening span between.
TAB-FULL:v15p582/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: {ما بين أيدينا} [مريم: 64] الآخرة {وما خلفنا} [مريم: 64] الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas places the afterlife before them and this world behind them.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {بين أيدينا} [مريم: 64] الآخرة {وما خلفنا} [مريم: 64] من الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r2.claim: Qatada says what is before them is the afterlife, what is behind is the world, and what is between is the span from this world to the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {له ما بين أيدينا} [مريم: 64] من أمر الآخرة {وما خلفنا} [مريم: 64] من أمر الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r3.claim: In another report, Qatada identifies what is between the two realms as the interval between the trumpet blasts.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {له ما بين أيدينا} [مريم: 64] من الآخرة {وما خلفنا} [مريم: 64] من الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also reads what is before them as the afterlife and what is behind them as this world.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ما بين أيدينا} [مريم: 64] من الآخرة

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the phrase covers what has passed before them, what will come after them in both worlds, and everything between those spans.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج، {ما بين أيدينا} [مريم: 64] قال: ما مضى أمامنا من الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r6.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r6.claim: Some Basran Arab grammarians interpret what is before as before creation, what is behind as after annihilation, and what is between as the time of existence.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r6.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة يتأول ذلك {له ما بين أيدينا} [مريم: 64] قبل أن نخلق

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that what is before them means the coming afterlife, what is behind means the past world, and what lies between spans now until the Resurrection; ordinary Arabic usage favors the future as before one.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r7.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب، قول من قال: معناه: له ما بين أيدينا من أمر الآخرة

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r8.claim: His argument is that “before you” most commonly denotes what has not yet arrived, while “behind” denotes what one has left; Qurʾānic interpretation follows the dominant sense unless evidence requires otherwise.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r8.anchor: فإن الأغلب في استعمال الناس إذا قالوا: هذا الأمر بين يديك

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r9.claim: In context, Gabriel tells Muhammad not to press him for delay: angels descend only by God’s order, for God owns and governs past, future, and the interval to the Hour.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r9.anchor: فلا تستبطئنا يا محمد في تخلفنا عنك، فإنا لا نتنزل من السماء إلى الأرض إلا بأمر ربك لنا بالنزول إليها

TAB-FULL:v15p583/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r10.claim: “Your Lord was not forgetful” means God does not forget Muhammad; nothing in heaven or earth escapes Him, and He knows what He decrees and governs.
TAB-FULL:v15p583/r10.anchor: ولم يكن ربك ذا نسيان، فيتأخر نزولي إليك بنسيانه إياك بل هو الذي لا يعزب عنه شيء في السماء ولا في الأرض

TAB-FULL:v15p584/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p584/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p584/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses “your Lord was not forgetful” as meaning that God has not forgotten you.
TAB-FULL:v15p584/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وما كان ربك نسيا} [مريم: 64] قال: ما نسيك ربك

TABATABAI:19:64-65/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r1.claim: These two verses interrupt the surrounding passage, yet their Qur’anic style indicates that they are Gabriel’s speech revealed by God; this supports reports that the Prophet asked why Gabriel’s coming was delayed and received this reply by revelation.
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r1.anchor: سياقهما يشهد بأنهما من كلام ملك الوحي بوحي قرآني من الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:19:64-65/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r2.claim: Reports, including one attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas in al-Majmaʿ, say the Prophet found Gabriel’s revelation delayed and asked him about it.
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r2.anchor: ورواه في مجمع البيان أيضا عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم استبطأ نزول جبريل

TABATABAI:19:64-65/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r3.claim: The author rejects proposed links that insert an implied statement by Gabriel, connect the verses to Gabriel’s earlier words to Mary, or put them in the mouths of the pious in Paradise; context and eloquence disfavor them.
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r3.anchor: وهي جميعا وجوه ظاهرة السخافة يأباها السياق ولا يقبلها النظم البليغ

TABATABAI:19:64-65/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r4.claim: Tanazzul means descending gradually; negation with exception restricts the angels’ descent to God’s command, in line with their never disobeying what He orders.
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r4.anchor: والنفي والاستثناء يفيدان الحصر فلا يتنزل

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r1.claim: One interpretation takes what is before the angels as the future, what is behind as the past, and what lies between as the present.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r1.anchor: فقيل المراد بما بين أيدينا ما هو قدامنا من الزمان المستقبل وبما خلفنا الماضي وبما بين ذلك الحال

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation makes what is before them the time before creation, what is behind them the period after death until the hereafter, and what is between their lifetime.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r2.anchor: ما خلفنا ما بعد الموت إلى استمرار الآخرة

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r3.claim: Another view divides time by the two trumpet blasts: before the first, after the second, and between them the forty years separating the blasts.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r3.anchor: الدنيا إلى النفخة الأولى وما خلفهم هو ما بعد النفخه الثانية

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r4.claim: Another view reverses the order, taking what is before them as the hereafter and what is behind them as this world.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r4.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم الآخرة وما خلفهم الدنيا

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r5.claim: Another view means pre-creation, post-annihilation, and the interval between worldly life and the hereafter.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r5.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم ما قبل الخلق وما خلفهم ما بعد الفناء وما بين ذلك ما بين الدنيا والآخرة

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation divides the world’s remaining time, its elapsed time, and the present period among the three phrases.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r6.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم ما بقي من أمر الدنيا وما خلفهم ما مضى منه وما بين ذلك ما هم فيه

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r7.claim: Another view refers to the beginning of creation, the ends of their lifespans, and the duration of their lives.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r7.anchor: ابتداء خلقنا ومنتهى آجالنا و مدة حياتنا

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r8.claim: One spatial interpretation places heaven ahead, earth behind, and the space between them in the middle phrase.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r8.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم السماء وما خلفهم الأرض وما بين ذلك ما بينهما

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r9.claim: Another spatial interpretation reverses heaven and earth’s positions in the first two phrases.

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r10.claim: Another spatial reading means the place to which angels move, the place from which they move, and the place where they are.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r10.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم المكان الذي ينتقلون إليه وما خلفهم المكان الذي ينتقلون منه

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r11.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r11.claim: A further view says the wording covers both time and place.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r11.anchor: وهناك قول بكون الآية تعم الزمان والمكان

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r12.claim: The author counts eleven interpretations but finds no evidence for them and objects that they measure angels by human categories; he instead reads the phrases as angels’ effects, their prior causes, and their own existence, encompassing them completely.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r12.anchor: فهذه أحد عشر قولا ولا دليل على شيء منها مع ما فيها من قياس الملك على الإنسان

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r13.claim: God’s ownership explains why angels descend only by command: their existence, antecedents, and effects all belong to Him, and they neither disobey nor will except with His permission.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r13.anchor: يفيد إحاطة ملكه تعالى بهم ملكا حقيقيا لا يجري فيه تصرف غيره ولا إرادة من سواه

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r14.claim: God’s comprehensive ownership explains the command restriction, while not being forgetful completes that rationale: nothing in His domain is neglected in His governance.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r14.anchor: من تمام التعليل أي إنه تعالى لا ينسى شيئا من ملكه

TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r15.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r15.claim: A reported reading says God did not forget or abandon His prophets; although it can fit one occasion report, it leaves the ownership phrase without its explanatory role and disconnects the next verse.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#2/r15.anchor: وقيل المعنى وما كان ربك نسيا أي تاركا لأنبيائه

TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r7.claim: Repeatedly addressing the angels’ speaker as your Lord prepares the declaration of oneness: the angels’ Lord is the Prophet’s Lord, so the call to worship is His; the surah’s opening has the same coherent aim.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r7.anchor: إشارة إلى أن ربنا الذي نتنزل عن أمره هو ربك

TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r1.claim: The proposed continuation makes the two verses confirm the preceding revelation: Gabriel was commanded to deliver the surah and then clarify that he descended only by God’s command, whose call is to worship the sole Lord.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r1.anchor: فكأن ملك الوحي لما تنزل عليه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالسورة وأوحى إليه الآيات الثلاث والستين

TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r2.claim: The king-and-messenger analogy shows how Gabriel’s explanatory words remain a message from God; this reading fits the verses better and more clearly than varying, weak occasion reports.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r2.anchor: وهذا نظير أن يرسل ملك رسولا بكتاب من عنده أو رسالة إلى بعض عماله

TABRISI:19:61-65/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:61-65/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:61-65/r7.claim: The phrase about descending only by God's command has an implied imperative qul, say.
TABRISI:19:61-65/r7.anchor: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك تقديره قل ما نتنزل فأضمر القول

TABRISI:19:61-65/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:61-65/r8.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:19:61-65/r8.claim: Abū ʿAlī reads what is before as past, what is behind as future, and what is between as the present.
TABRISI:19:61-65/r8.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أن الأزمنة ثلاثة ماض وهو قوله ما بين أيدينا

TABRISI:19:61-65/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:61-65/r11.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك وقتادة والكلبي ومقاتل
TABRISI:19:61-65/r11.claim: Revelation paused after questions about the Cave Companions, Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; the Prophet reproached Gabriel for delay, and this verse answered him.
TABRISI:19:61-65/r11.anchor: احتبس الوحي أياما لما سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قصة أصحاب الكهف

TABRISI:19:62-64/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:62-64/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:62-64/r9.claim: When the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often, Gabriel said angels descend only when God commands; others also transmit this.
TABRISI:19:62-64/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لجبرائيل ما منعك أن تزورنا أكثر

TABRISI:19:62-64/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:62-64/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:19:62-64/r10.claim: Alternatively, the speakers are people of Paradise, who descend to a place there only by God's command.
TABRISI:19:62-64/r10.anchor: وقيل: إنه قول أهل الجنة إنا لا نتنزل موضعا من الجنة إلا بأمر الله تعالى

TABRISI:19:62-64/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:62-64/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك والربيع
TABRISI:19:62-64/r11.claim: What is ahead is the Hereafter, what is behind is past worldly life, and what lies between is the interval between trumpet blasts.
TABRISI:19:62-64/r11.anchor: ما بين أيدينا من أمر الآخرة وما خلفنا أي ما مضى من أمر الدنيا

TABRISI:19:62-64/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:62-64/r12.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:19:62-64/r12.claim: Muqātil says the interval between the two blasts is forty years.
TABRISI:19:62-64/r12.anchor: قال مقاتل: وما بين النفختين أربعون سنة

TABRISI:19:62-64/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:62-64/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:62-64/r13.claim: Other readings cover all created life, past and remaining worldly affairs plus present life, or earth, heaven, and what lies between.
TABRISI:19:62-64/r13.anchor: وقيل: معناه ابتداء خلقنا ومنتهى آجالنا ومدة حياتنا

TABRISI:19:62-64/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:62-64/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:62-64/r14.claim: The statement that God is not forgetful may conclude the angels' or Paradise dwellers' words; alternatively God says He does not forget Muhammad during a delay in revelation.
TABRISI:19:62-64/r14.anchor: قيل هذا تمام حكاية قول الملائكة وقول أهل الجنة

THALABI:v6p222/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p222/r2.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v6p222/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often, and this verse was revealed.
THALABI:v6p222/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا جبرئيل ما يمنعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا

THALABI:v6p222/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p222/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p222/r3.claim: Mujahid says Gabriel delayed, then asked why the Muslims did not trim nails, shorten moustaches, or use tooth-sticks; the verse was revealed.
THALABI:v6p222/r3.anchor:
وقال مجاهد: أبطأت الرسل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أتاه جبرئيل فقال:
ما حبسك

THALABI:v6p222/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p222/r4.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك ومقاتل وقتادة والكلبي
THALABI:v6p222/r4.claim: They say Gabriel’s visit was delayed while the Prophet awaited answers about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; the delay distressed him and pagans said his Lord had forsaken him.
THALABI:v6p222/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة والضحاك ومقاتل وقتادة والكلبي: احتبس جبرئيل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين سأله قومه عن قصة أصحاب الكهف

THALABI:v6p222/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p222/r5.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v6p222/r5.claim: ʿIkrima says Gabriel’s delay lasted forty days.

THALABI:v6p222/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p222/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p222/r6.claim: Mujahid says the delay lasted twelve nights; another view says fifteen.
THALABI:v6p222/r6.anchor:
وقال مجاهد: اثنتي عشرة ليلة وقيل:
خمس عشرة

THALABI:v6p222/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p222/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p222/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes these words the speech of Paradise’s inhabitants, saying the gardens descend only by God’s command.
THALABI:v6p222/r7.anchor: وقيل: هذا إخبار عن أهل الجنة، أنهم يقولون عند دخولها: ما تتنزل هذه الجنان إلا بأمر الله

THALABI:v6p222/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p222/r8.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p222/r8.claim: Muqatil explains what is before the angels as the afterlife, what is behind them as worldly life, and what is between as the period between the two trumpet blasts—forty years.
THALABI:v6p222/r8.anchor: قال مقاتل: له ما بين أيدينا من أمر الآخرة وما خلفنا من أمر الدنيا وما بين ذلك يعني بين النفختين

THALABI:v6p222/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p222/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p222/r9.claim: Other explanations identify the domains as creation, the end of lifespans, and lifetime; or the afterlife’s reward and punishment, past deeds, and what remains until Resurrection.
THALABI:v6p222/r9.anchor: وقيل: كان له ابتداء خلقنا وله كان منتهى آجالنا، وله كان مدة حياتنا

THALABI:v6p222/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p222/r10.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v6p222/r10.claim: The Prophet told Gabriel that the delay caused him distress and longing; Gabriel replied that he descends only when commanded and remains absent when held back.
THALABI:v6p222/r10.anchor: قال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أبطأت علي حتى ساء ظني واشتقت إليك

THALABI:v6p223/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p223/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p223/r1.claim: Further readings of “what is before and behind us” cover afterlife recompense, past worldly deeds, and all that will happen before Resurrection; another view means before creation, after death, and present life.
THALABI:v6p223/r1.anchor: ويقال: ما بين أيدينا من الثواب والعقاب وأمور الآخرة وما خلفنا ما مضى من أعمالنا في الدنيا

THALABI:v6p223/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p223/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p223/r2.claim: For the angels, the phrase can refer to earth, heaven, and what lies between; all belong to God, so nothing can be done except by His command.
THALABI:v6p223/r2.anchor: ويقال له ما بين أيدينا إلى الأرض إذا أردنا النزول إليها وما خلفنا أي السماء إذا نزلنا منها

THALABI:v6p223/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p223/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p223/r3.claim: God is not forgetful: when He wills to send a revelation, He sends it.
THALABI:v6p223/r3.anchor: وما كان ربك نسيا أي ناسيا إذا شاء أن يرسل إليك أرسل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r1.claim: When the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often, this verse was revealed in reply.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r1.anchor: روي بطرق كثيره عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس: (أن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال لجبريل:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r2.claim: After the Prophet promised answers about Dhul-Qarnayn, the Cave Companions, and the Spirit without saying God willing, revelation was delayed forty days; Gabriel returned after 18:23–24 and the Prophet asked why he had not visited.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r2.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: (سأل المشركون رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- عن ذي القرنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r3.claim: They say the Prophet missed Gabriel; Gabriel replied that he too longed for Muhammad but was a commanded servant who descended when sent and stayed when held.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p279/r3.anchor: والمفسرون كلهم [في سبب نزول] (¬4) هذه الآية على هذا، قالوا: (استبطأ رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r1.claim: What is before us means the Hereafter and what is behind us means the worldly life; Sufyan, Qatada, and Muqatil agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: ({له ما بين أيدينا} من أمر الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r2.speaker: السدي ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r2.claim: They reverse the first pair: before us means this world and behind us the Hereafter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r2.anchor: وقال الآخرون: {له ما بين أيدينا} الدنيا {وما خلفنا} الآخرة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r3.claim: What is between those is the interval between worldly life and the Hereafter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r3.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: (ما بين الدنيا والآخرة) (¬6). وهو قول مجاهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r4.claim: In al-Layth’s narration, what is between them means the period between the two trumpet blasts; al-Suddi, Qatada, Sufyan, al-Rabiʿ, al-Dahhak, and Abu al-ʿAliya agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r4.anchor: وهو قول مجاهد في رواية ابن أبي نجيح (¬7). وقال في رواية # الليث: (وما بين ذلك ما بين النفختين)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r5.claim: Before us is the Hereafter’s reward and punishment, behind us is all past worldly life, and between them is the time from now until Resurrection; this is preferred because the two blasts have not yet been mentioned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: ({ما بين أيدينا} من أمر الآخرة والثواب والعقاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r6.claim: In Ata’s narration, before us is the earth, behind us the heavens, and between them the air; everything belongs to God and can occur only by His command.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p280/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: ({له ما بين أيدينا} يريد الدنيا يعني الأرض.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r1.claim: God did not leave the Prophet when revelation was delayed; nasiya here means one who forgets or abandons.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد تاركا لك منذ أبطاء عنك الوحي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r2.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r2.claim: God did not forget the Prophet.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r3.claim: When revelation paused, polytheists said God had forgotten and abandoned Muhammad; this verse and 93:3 were revealed against them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r3.anchor: وذلك أن المشركين قالوا لما أبطأ عنه الوحي: قد نسيه وودعه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r4.claim: God knows and preserves everything past, present, and future, forgetting none of it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (أي قد علم الله ما كان وما يكون وما هو كائن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r2.claim: Gabriel had been absent from the Prophet for days; the Prophet asked why he had not visited, and this revelation followed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r2.anchor: كان جبريل عليه السلام قد احتبس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أياما، فلما نزل قال له: ألا زرتنا، فأنزل الله سبحانه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r3.claim: One explanation says what is before is the afterlife, what is behind is past worldly affairs, and what is between is the present until Resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r3.anchor: له ما بين أيدينا } من أمر الآخرة [ { وما خلفنا } ما مضى من أمر الدنيا] { وما بين ذلك } ما يكون من هذا الوقت إلى قيام الساعة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r4.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r4.claim: Another explanation takes what is before as the world, what is behind as the heavens, and what is between as the air.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r4.anchor: وقيل: { له ما بين أيدينا }: يعني: الدنيا، { وما خلفنا } يعني: السموات، { وما بين ذلك }: الهواء:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r5.claim: God is not forgetful or one who abandons the Prophet during delayed revelation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r5.anchor: وما كان ربك نسيا } تاركا لك منذ أبطأ عنك الوحي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p233/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p233/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p233/r3.claim: Qatāda says the statement about descending only by the Lord's command is Gabriel speaking; after a pause in revelation, Gabriel tells the Prophet that the affairs ahead belong to God and means the afterlife.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p233/r3.anchor: سعيد عن قتادة قال: هذا قول جبريل. احتبس عن النبي في بعض الوحي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r1.claim: Al-Suddī interprets what lies behind the angels as worldly affairs, in the circumstance of being in the afterlife.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r1.anchor: وما خلفنا} [مريم: 64] من أمر الدنيا، وهو تفسير السدي، أي إذا كنا في الآخرة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r2.claim: What lies between the two is the affairs of this world and the next.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r2.anchor: وما بين ذلك} [مريم: 64] من أمر الدنيا والآخرة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r3.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the interval between as the barzakh between the two trumpet blasts.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هو البرزخ، يعني: ما بين النفختين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r4.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r4.claim: Al-Suddī reads what is before and behind us as what preceded our creation and what comes after it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: {له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا} [مريم: 64] يعني ما كان قبل خلقنا وما يكون بعد خلقنا

ELMALILI:19:59-63/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:19:59-63/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:19:59-63/r2.claim: The repeated taqī ending recalls Maryam’s earlier story; as Gabriel spoke there, Gabriel’s speech will follow here as well.
ELMALILI:19:59-63/r2.anchor: Burada işbu تَقِيًّۭا fâsılasının tekerrürü tâ yukarıda Meryem kıssasında geçen تَقِيًّۭا fâsılasını hatırlatır.

ELMALILI:19:59-63/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:19:59-63/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:19:59-63/r3.claim: The spirit who told Maryam he was her Lord’s messenger is Gabriel, and here he answers Muhammad’s question about why he visits less often.
ELMALILI:19:59-63/r3.anchor: Orada Meryem’e إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ diyen rûh, yani Cebrâil burada Resûlullah’ın bir suâline cevâben demiştir ki

ELMALILI:19:64-65/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:19:64-65/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:19:64-65/r1.claim: The opening waw is resumptive, and the verse answers a question whose occasion is known from the reports about its revelation.
ELMALILI:19:64-65/r1.anchor: Buradaki vâv, istînâfiyedir. Yani bir suâle cevaptır ki bu sual, sebeb-i nüzûlünden mâlum olabiliyor.

ELMALILI:19:64-65/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:19:64-65/r2.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:19:64-65/r2.claim: Elmalılı cites Ahmad, Bukhari, Tirmidhi, Nasa’i, and others: Muhammad asked Gabriel why he visited less often, and this verse was revealed.
ELMALILI:19:64-65/r2.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem “yâ Cibrîl, bizi ziyaret ettiğinden daha çok ziyaret etmeye ne mâni‘oluyor?” demişti

ELMALILI:19:64-65/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:19:64-65/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:19:64-65/r3.claim: Elmalılı takes the verse as Gabriel’s answer; the occasion and content support this, as does the repeated taqī ending recalling Gabriel as the spirit mentioned earlier in the sura.
ELMALILI:19:64-65/r3.anchor: Demek ki bu âyet, Cebrâil’in o suâle cevâbını hikâyedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r1.speaker: Abdullah b. Abbas
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel to visit him more often, and these verses were revealed in response.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r1.anchor: Abdullah b. Abbas’tan rivayet edildiğine göre Resulullah, Cebrâil’in kendisini daha çok ziyaret etmesini istemiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r2.claim: Another report says Quraysh questioned the Prophet, he promised a near answer, and when Gabriel was delayed they claimed his Lord had forgotten him; the Prophet grieved and these verses followed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r2.anchor: inkârcılar Hz. Peygamber’e bazı konularda sorular sormuşlar; Peygamber efendimiz de kendilerine yakında bilgi vereceğini söylemiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r3.speaker: Müfessirlerin genel kabulü
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r3.claim: The prevailing exegetical view is that these are God's words, commanding Gabriel to answer the Prophet accordingly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r3.anchor: Müfessirlerin genel kabulüne göre bu iki âyet Allah’ın sözü olup Cebrâil’e, Hz. Peygamber’e böyle cevap vermesini emretmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r4.claim: The free rendering says angels descend only at their Lord's command; all places and times belong to God, and delayed revelation reflects wisdom rather than forgetfulness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r4.anchor: Onun emri ve iradesi olmadan biz hiçbir zaman ve hiçbir yerde hareket edemeyiz

SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r1.claim: Ibn ‘Atiyya says the waw links one sentence to another and connects the statements despite their differing meanings.
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " الواو عاطفة جملة كلام على أخرى، واصلة بين القولين

SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r2.speaker: النقاش
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r2.claim: Al-Naqqash unusually links وما نتنزل to the angels’ statement in 19:19, قال إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك.
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r2.anchor: وقد أغرب النقاش في حكايته لقول: وهو أن قوله { وما نتنزل } ، متصل بقوله

SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa’ makes وما نتنزل dependent on an omitted statement-introducing verb: ‘and the angels say.’
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r3.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " وما نتنزل، أي: وتقول الملائكة " فجعله معمولا لقول مضمر.

SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r4.claim: Another view makes the words a statement by the people of Paradise, which the author considers closer than the preceding interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو من كلام أهل الجنة وهو أقرب مما قبله.

SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r5.claim: نتنزل is the reflexive of form-II نزل; it may imply gradual descent over time, though it need not, and al-Zamakhshari distinguishes gradual descent from descent generally.
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r5.anchor: ونتنزل مطاوع نزل بالتشديد ويقتضي العمل في مهلة وقد لا يقتضيها.

SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari prefers gradual descent here: the angels descend at intervals, one time after another; he cites a line about an angel descending from the sky.
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r6.anchor: واللائق بهذا الموضع هو النزول على مهل، والمراد: أن نزولنا في الأحايين وقتا غب وقت ".

SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r7.claim: The common reading uses first-person plural نون; al-A‘raj reads third-person singular ياء.
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r7.anchor: وقرأ العامة " نتنزل " بنون الجمع. وقرأ الأعرج " يتنزل " بياء الغيبة.

SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r8.claim: For the yā’ reading, Ibn ‘Atiyya identifies the subject as Gabriel but says the following ‘to Him belongs what is before us’ resists that construction unless it is a quotation.
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r8.anchor: أحدهما: أنه ضمير جبريل. قال ابن عطية: " ويرده قوله " له لما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا "

SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead takes the yā’ subject as revelation, quoted from Gabriel; this too requires an implicit saying that introduces the following words.
SAMIN-DURR:19:64/r9.anchor: الثاني: أنه يعود على الوحي، وكذا قال الزمخشري على الحكاية عن جبريل، والضمير للوحي،

SAMIN-DURR:19:64#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:64#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:64#2/r1.claim: Some grammarians infer from this verse that time has three divisions—past, present, and future—and compare the cited line by Zuhayr contrasting knowledge of today and yesterday with tomorrow.
SAMIN-DURR:19:64#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { له ما بين أيدينا } استدل بعض النحاة على أن الأزمنة ثلاثة: ماض وحاضر ومستقبل بهذه الآية،

ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r1.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r1.claim: A report says Gabriel delayed bringing revelation, and the Prophet told him that he had been missed; Gabriel answered with this verse.
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r1.anchor: يروى أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أبطأ عنه جبريل عليه السلام في الوحي، فقال عليه السلام وقد أتاه جبريل: ما زرتنا حتى اشتقت إليك

ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r2.claim: What lies ahead is the afterlife's reward and punishment; what is behind is all past worldly events; what is between is from now until Resurrection.
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r2.anchor: ما بين أيدينا امر الآخرة والثواث والعقاب، وما خلفنا جميع ما مضى من أمر الدنيا

ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r3.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes “what is between” as the interval between the two trumpet blasts.
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r3.anchor: وجاء في التفسير وما بين ذلك قيل ما بين النفختين

ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r4.claim: God is not forgetful: He knows past, present, and future and preserves them all.
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r4.anchor: أي قد علم الله جل وعلا ما كان وما يكون وما هو كائن، حافظ لذلك عز وجل.

ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r5.claim: It may also reassure the Prophet that his Lord had not forgotten him despite the revelation's delay.
ZAJJAJ:v3p337/r5.anchor: وجائز أن يكون والله أعلم: ما نسيك ربك وإن تأخر عنك الوحي.

ASAD-NOTES:19:62#n50/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:62#n50/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:62#n50/r1.claim: The angels' knowledge of what is before, behind, and between is limited: they can glimpse it but cannot fully understand it.
ASAD-NOTES:19:62#n50/r1.anchor: that which even the angels can only glimpse but not fully understand

ASAD-NOTES:19:62#n50/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:62#n50/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:62#n50/r2.claim: The angel reference connects with the preceding prophets because they, like Muhammad, received divine revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:19:62#n50/r2.anchor: The reference to the angels connects with the preceding mention of some of the earlier prophets who, like Muhammad, were recipients of divine revelation

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p10#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p10#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p10#3/r1.claim: Qatada says Gabriel had delayed visiting the Prophet; when the Prophet felt the delay, Gabriel replied that angels descend only by God's command.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p10#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قال لبث جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما أتاه وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد استبطأه فقال له جبريل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p10#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p10#3/r2.speaker: جبريل
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p10#3/r2.claim: Gabriel explains that what lies ahead is the afterlife, what lies behind is worldly life, and what lies between is the period between the two blasts.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p10#3/r2.anchor: يقول له ما بين أيدينا في الآخرة وما خلفنا من الدنيا وما بين ذلك يقول ما بين النفختين

TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r3.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r3.claim: Al-Rida says God neither forgets nor slips; forgetting by God means recompensing those who forgot him by making them forget themselves or leaving them as they neglected preparation for meeting him, as 19:64, 39:19, and 45:34 explain.
TABATABAI:9:64-74#8/r3.anchor: قال سألت الرضا عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { نسوا الله فنسيهم } فقال إن الله تبارك وتعالى لا ينسى

BAQILLANI:v1p44/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r1.claim: The letters opening sūras include half the letters within several Arabic classifications, including strong versus nonstrong and emphatic versus open letters.
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r1.anchor: وقد علمنا أن نصف هذه الحروف في جملة تلك الحروف المبدوء بها في أوائل السور

BAQILLANI:v1p44/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r2.claim: Because later classifiers found this balanced selection in the sūra openings, its placement is beyond chance and signals divine knowledge of the unseen.
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r2.anchor: لا يجوز أن يقع إلا من الله عز وجل لأن ذلك يجري مجرى علم الغيوب

BAQILLANI:v1p44/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r3.claim: Whether Arabic was divinely instituted or formed by convention, the ordered structure of its letters is remarkable and reflects wisdom beyond ordinary capacity.
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r3.anchor: فإن كان أصل اللغة توقيفا فالأمر في ذلك أبين وإن كان على سبيل التواضع فهو عجيب أيضا

BAQILLANI:v1p44/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r4.claim: In alif-lām-mīm, alif is articulated farthest away, lām midway, and mīm at the lips; naming them signals the full range of familiar letters used in the Qurʾānic composition.
BAQILLANI:v1p44/r4.anchor: لأن الألف المبدوء بها هي أقصاها مطلا واللام متوسطة والميم متطرفة لأنها تأخذ في الشفة

BURHAN:v2p509/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p509/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p509/r3.claim: The pattern فعيل often marks intensive or repeated active meaning—رحيم, سميع, قدير, and similar forms—rather than an object, as shown by قتيل and جريح, whose killing or wounding is not gradable.
BURHAN:v2p509/r3.anchor: وأما فعيل فعند النحاة أنه من صيغ المبالغة والتكرار كرحيم وسميع وقدير

BURHAN:v2p509/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p509/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p509/r5.claim: A problem is raised: negating the intensive نسيا does not logically negate any forgetfulness. The author points to the suitability of the phrase for the preceding verse endings and promises further answers.
BURHAN:v2p509/r5.anchor: ومن المشكل ﴿ وما كان ربك نسيا ﴾ فإن النفي متوجه على الخبر

BURHAN:v2p82/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p82/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p82/r1.claim: The preceding position is approved by scholars because it avoids both anthropomorphism and negation; the Throne is uniquely eminent, the first creation, surrounded by angels, linked to the station of nearness, and the roof of Paradise.
BURHAN:v2p82/r1.anchor: وهذا قول مرضي عند العلماء لسلامته من التشبيه والتعطيل وللعرش خصوصية ليست لغيره

BURHAN:v2p375/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p375/r2.speaker: ابن الشجري
BURHAN:v2p375/r2.claim: Ibn al-Shajari distinguishes truthful negation (nafy) from denial known to be false (jahd); nafy is broader, so every jahd is nafy but not vice versa.
BURHAN:v2p375/r2.anchor: قال ابن الشجري ان كان النافي صادقا فيما قاله سمي كلامه نفيا وان كان يعلم كذب ما نفاه كان جحدا

BURHAN:v2p375/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p375/r3.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURHAN:v2p375/r3.claim: Some scholars do not distinguish nafy from jahd; the author prefers Ibn al-Shajari’s distinction.
BURHAN:v2p375/r3.anchor: قال ومن العلماء من لايفرق بينهما والاصل ماذكرته

BURHAN:v2p375/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p375/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p375/r4.claim: Negation is half of all speech, since speech is either affirmation or negation.
BURHAN:v2p375/r4.anchor: هو شطر الكلام كله لان الكلام اما اثبات أو نفي

BURHAN:v2p375/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p375/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p375/r5.claim: The author rejects the claim that sound negation requires the negated attribute to be possible, and the Hanafi inference that prohibition therefore entails validity; negation can deny rational impossibility or a possible event that does not occur.
BURHAN:v2p375/r5.anchor: والصواب ان انتفاء الشيء عن الشيء قد يكون لكونه لا يمكن منه عقلا

BURHAN:v2p375/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p375/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p375/r6.claim: The negated element is what immediately follows the negation particle: ما ضربت زيدا denies the act, while ما أنا ضربته denies that I was its agent.
BURHAN:v2p375/r6.anchor: المنفي ما ولى حرف النفي فاذا قلت ماضربت زيدا كنت نافيا للفعل

ITQAN:v1p102#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p102#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p102#2/r3.claim: The statement that the angels descend only by their Lord’s command is spoken by Gabriel.

ITQAN:v3p240#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p240#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p240#2/r3.claim: The phrase exhausts the divisions of time into what lies ahead, behind, and between, leaving no fourth category.
ITQAN:v3p240#2/r3.anchor: وكذا قوله تعالى ﴿ له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك ﴾ استوفى أقسام الزمان ولا رابع لهما

ITQAN:v3p208/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p208/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v3p208/r1.claim: Some require that a thing be capable of an attribute for its negation to be valid; the cited divine negations disprove that requirement.
ITQAN:v3p208/r1.anchor: زعم بعضهم أن شرط صحة النفي عن الشيء صحة اتصاف المنفي عنه بذلك الشيء وهو مردود بقوله تعالى ﴿ وما ربك بغافل عما يعملون ﴾

ITQAN:v3p208/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p208/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p208/r2.claim: Negation can apply either because the attribute is logically impossible for the subject or because it is possible but does not occur; the cited verse supplies the latter kind of formulation.
ITQAN:v3p208/r2.anchor: والصواب أن انتفاء الشيء عن الشيء قد يكون لكونه لا يمكن منه عقلا وقد يكون لكونه لا يقع منه مع إمكانه

ITQAN:v3p209#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p209#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p209#3/r1.claim: Negating a general term entails negating its particulars, while affirming a general term does not establish every particular; affirming a particular establishes the general, but negating one particular does not negate the general.
ITQAN:v3p209#3/r1.anchor: نفي العام يدل على نفي الخاص وثبوته لا يدل على ثبوته وثبوت الخاص يدل على ثبوت العام ونفيه لا يدل على نفيه

ITQAN:v3p209#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p209#3/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p209#3/r5.claim: A related rule is that denying an intensive form does not automatically deny the basic act; the source treats ظلام and نسي as apparent counterexamples needing explanation.
ITQAN:v3p209#3/r5.anchor: ونظير هذه القاعدة أن نفي المبالغة في الفعل لا يستلزم نفي أصل الفعل وقد أشكل على هذا آيتان

ITQAN:v3p269/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p269/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p269/r1.claim: The Qur’an sometimes uses an intensive form such as ʿalim or qadir while elsewhere using the basic forms ʿalim and qadir; the catalog includes nasiyyan.
ITQAN:v3p269/r1.anchor: السابع والعشرون الإتيان بصيغة المبالغة كقدير وعليم مع ترك ذلك في نحو هو القادر وعالم الغيب ومنه ﴿ وما كان ربك نسيا ﴾

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r1.claim: Taking the bow by its maker means the taking is appropriate to the person and object; the likeness concerns the resulting judgment, not the act of taking alone.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r1.anchor: أخذ القوس باريها وذلك أن المعنى على وقوع الأخذ في موقعه ووجوده من أهله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r2.claim: The saying about twisting at the camel's hump means persuading someone from refusal to agreement; the resemblance belongs to twisting when applied to that object, not twisting by itself.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r2.anchor: ما زال يفتل منه في الذروة والغارب الشبه مأخوذ بين الفتل وما تعدى إليه من الذروة والغارب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r3.claim: The likeness can depend on a direct object, a prepositional phrase, or a circumstantial clause: writing in water and a camel driver without a camel each need the accompanying phrase.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r3.anchor: المفعول كالقوس في قولك أخذ القوس باريها وما يجرى مجرى المفعول الجار مع المجرور

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r4.claim: Some comparisons require both an object and its prepositional setting, as gathering two swords in one sheath or hunting in a lion's den.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r4.anchor: وهل يجمع السيفان في الغمد وآنت كمن يجمع السيفين في غمد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r5.claim: Thus this kind of likeness needs a full clause or a clause-like equivalent, which can be expressed with a verbal noun or an active participle.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p85/r5.anchor: لا بدد لك في هذا الضرب من الشبه من جملة صريحة أو حكم الجملة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r1.claim: The Prophet listened to poetry and had Ḥassān, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa, and Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr praise him and answer the polytheists in verse.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r1.anchor: فقد كان حسان وعبد الله بن رواحة وكعب بن زهير يمدحونه ، ويسمع منهم ويصغي إليهم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet told Kaʿb that God had not forgotten a poem he wrote, then had Abū Bakr recite the line about Sukayna’s claim to overcome her Lord.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r2.anchor: ما نسي ربك وما كان ربك نسيا شعرا قلته

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r3.claim: At the Prophet’s rain prayer, Abū Ṭālib’s poem praised him as a white-faced intercessor for rain and protector of orphans and widows.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r3.anchor: الخبر المعروف في استنشاده - حين استسقى فسقي - قول أبي طالب ، + الكامل + :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r4.speaker: عبد الله
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r4.claim: Abd Allāh reports that at Badr the Prophet said Abū Ṭālib, if alive, would know their swords had reached the enemy; he cited Abū Ṭālib’s earlier verse predicting the swords would be seized.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r4.anchor: وعن الشعبي رضي الله عنه عن مسروق ، عن عبد الله قال : لما نظر رسول الله إلى القتلى يوم بدر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r5.speaker: محمد بن مسلمة الأنصاري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r5.claim: Muḥammad ibn Maslama reports that the Prophet asked Ḥassān for al-Aʿshā’s pre-Islamic satire, then forbade it after learning al-Aʿshā had praised him to Caesar; he praised gratitude to people as gratitude to God. No grading is given.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p33/r5.anchor: ومن المحفوظ في ذلك حديث محمد بن مسلمة الأنصاري ؛

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p548/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p548/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p548/r1.claim: Between one’s hands means in front and behind means at the rear; these are physical meanings that can be extended metaphorically.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p548/r1.anchor: ما بين أيديهم : هو القدام . وما خلفهم : هو الوراء والخلف والأصل معرفة هذا بالذوات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p548/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p548/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p548/r4.claim: A third use contrasts the afterlife ahead with worldly life behind; Satan approaches from worldly temptations in front and denies resurrection from behind.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p548/r4.anchor: والثالث : ما بين أيديهم : الآخرة . وما خلفهم : الدنيا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p182/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p182/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p182/r1.claim: The author counts twenty-three singular predicates after laysa with the extra bāʾ, against only three without it: 4:94, 11:8, and 13:43.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p182/r1.anchor: ثلاثا وعشرين آية، في مقابل ثلاث آيات فحسب، جاء فيها خبر ليس غير مقترن بالباء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p182/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p182/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p182/r2.claim: With negative mā followed by kāna, the explicit singular predicate is usually unmarked by bāʾ; the author lists this verse among the examples.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p182/r2.anchor: "ما" الصريح المفرد يأتي غالباً مقترناً بالباء المقول بزيادتها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p37/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p37/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p37/r1.claim: Maryam's wording suits the context of God's ownership, provision, and inheritance; Ayat al-Kursi instead concerns knowledge, so “He knows what is before and behind them” prepares for the limit on their knowledge.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p37/r1.anchor: في سورة مريم سياق الآيات عن الملك (ولهم رزقهم فيها، تلك الجنة التي نورث من عبادنا، رب السموات والأرض..) الذي يرزق هو الذي يورّث فهو مالك

NASHR:v2p407/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p407/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p407/r1.claim: A strange report says that after the Prophet rebuked a persistent beggar, revelation stopped for forty mornings; Gabriel then brought al-Duha, and the Prophet ordered takbir after its opening through each surah's end. Ibn Abi Bazzah alone transmits it, and it is muʿḍal.
NASHR:v2p407/r1.anchor: وهو مما انفرد به ابن أبي بزة أيضا، وهو معضل.

NASHR:v2p407/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p407/r2.speaker: قتادة
NASHR:v2p407/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the words as Gabriel's reply after revelation had paused: he descends only at his Lord's command.
NASHR:v2p407/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: هذا قول جبريل عليه السلام

NASHR:v2p407/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p407/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v2p407/r3.claim: Al-Awfi reports from Ibn Abbas that Gabriel's delay distressed the Prophet, prompting the polytheists to say his Lord had abandoned and hated him; God answered with al-Duha's reassurance.
NASHR:v2p407/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - لما نزل على رسول الله

NASHR:v2p407/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p407/r4.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v2p407/r4.claim: Al-Dani says the delay explains why takbir was attached specifically to the close of al-Duha; Meccans kept the practice, while others followed the Prophet's later abandonment of it.
NASHR:v2p407/r4.anchor: قال الداني: فهذا سبب التخصيص بالتكبير من آخر والضحى

IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r1.claim: After a pause in revelation, Muhammad told Gabriel he had suspected him; Gabriel replied that angels descend only by God's command, and the opening of al-Kahf then answered Quraysh's challenge to Muhammad's prophethood.
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: فذكر لي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لجبريل حين جاءه

BUKHARI:3218/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:3218/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BUKHARI:3218/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Muhammad asked Gabriel why he did not visit more often; the verse was revealed to explain that the angels descend only by their Lord’s command.
BUKHARI:3218/r1.anchor: عَنْ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِجِبْرِيلَ

BUKHARI:4731/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4731/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BUKHARI:4731/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Muhammad asking Gabriel what kept him from visiting more often; the verse then answers that their descent occurs only by God’s command.
BUKHARI:4731/r1.anchor: عَنْ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

BUKHARI:7455/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7455/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BUKHARI:7455/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Muhammad asking Gabriel why he visited less often; the collection identifies the revealed verse as God’s answer to Muhammad.
BUKHARI:7455/r1.anchor: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا جِبْرِيلُ

IBNHIBBAN:2779/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2779/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNHIBBAN:2779/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that careful ablution, attending and listening at Friday prayer earns forgiveness through the next Friday plus three days; handling pebbles is idle conduct.
IBNHIBBAN:2779/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من توضأ فأحسن الوضوء، ثم أتى الجمعة فسمع وأنصت غفر له ما بين الجمعة إلى الجمعة وزيادة ثلاثة أيام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r5.claim: The passage’s insertion resembles 19:64 and the prayer command in 2:238, which appears amid the marriage rulings of al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r5.anchor: فيكون وقوع هذه الآية في هذه السورة مثل وقوع { وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك } في سورة مريم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.claim: The Prophet fixed the order of Quranic verses according to revelation, and that distinctive arrangement contributes to the Quran’s inimitability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.anchor: فلم تختلف قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ترتيب آي السور على نحو ما هو في المصحف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.claim: Reordering verses within a sura would destroy the inimitable style; the Prophet’s recitation followed the arrangement preserved in the present codex and confirmed in the final review.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.anchor: لو غير عنه إلى ترتيب آخر لنزل على حد الإعجاز الذي امتاز به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.claim: The arrangement was transmitted by companion memorizers from the Prophet’s final recitations; Zayd did not depart from it when compiling the codex for Abu Bakr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.anchor: استقرت عليه رواية الحفاظ من الصحابة عن العرضات الأخيرة التي كان يقرأ بها النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.claim: Muslims preserved the Quran chiefly through memorized recitation in prayers and other occasions; scribes wrote revelations on the Prophet’s command, and writing may have been intended as recourse in case of doubt or forgetting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.anchor: حفظ القرآن كل من حفظه كلا أو بعضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.claim: The companions are not reported to have disputed the order of any sura’s verses or objected to the collected Quran; it matched their memorization.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.anchor: لم يؤثر عنهم أنهم فرددوا في ترتيب آيات من إحدى السور ولا أثر عنهم إنكار أو اختلاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.claim: Ibn Wahb reports hearing Malik say that the Quran was arranged in the order in which people heard it from the Messenger of God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.anchor: سمعت مالكا يقول : إنما ألف القرآن على ما كانوا يسمعونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Gabriel showed the Prophet where a verse belonged, including verses revealed in response to a question; the arrangement of letters, verses, and suras came from the Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.anchor: كانت الآية تنزل جوابا لمستخبر يسأل ويوقف جبريل رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.claim: Normally, a verse relates to the one after it through a shared purpose, transition, or another form of connected discourse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.anchor: فلهذا كان الأصل في آي القرآن أن يكون بين الآية ولاحقتها تناسب في الغرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.claim: Conjunctions such as fa, lakin, and bal, and exception particles, signal connection but do not prove that adjacent passages were revealed in that order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.anchor: على أن وجود ذلك لا يعين اتصال ما بعده بما قبله في النزول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.speaker: بعض مشايخنا المحققين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.claim: A verified teacher of al-Zarkashi rejects the claim that one should not seek verse connections: first ask whether each verse completes the previous one or stands independently, then seek its relation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.anchor: قال بدر الدين الزركشي بعض مشايخنا المحققين قد وهم من قال لا تطلب للآي الكريمة مناسبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.claim: Gabriel reportedly paused revelation for days; after he resumed with the preceding verses of Mary, the Prophet reproached him and God directed him to answer with 19:64.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.anchor: جبريل لبث أياما لم ينزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بوحي

MUSNAD-AHMAD:2078/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2078/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2078/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often; 19:64 came down as the answer, explaining that the angels descend only by their Lord's command.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2078/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبريل عليه السلام: " ألا تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا؟ "

MUSNAD-AHMAD:3365/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3365/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3365/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet asking Gabriel why he does not visit more; 19:64 descended as the answer to Muhammad, placing Gabriel's visits under God's command.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3365/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبريل: " ما يمنعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا؟ "

TIRMIDHI:3158/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3158/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TIRMIDHI:3158/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel why he visited less often; 19:64 was then revealed. Al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan gharib.
TIRMIDHI:3158/r1.anchor: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِجِبْرِيلَ
